Striking open the silver world at will, the jade light of Mount Emei floats forth.

Mañjuśrī, clad in grass garments, son of the Dharma King and teacher of the seven Buddhas, entered Vaiśālī to inquire after the illness of Vimalakīrti; wielding the sword of wisdom, he severed [all delusions].
To resolve the doubts of the followers of the Two Vehicles, he extends his golden arm to welcome Sudhana; facing the Unattached One, he raises aloft a crystal vessel.
He scatters his hair like green clouds three thousand *zhang* long and dons robes of the eight auspicious fragrant herbs. Upon Mount Tai, snowflakes fall even in the sixth month;
with such majestic prowess, he truly rivals the lion’s cub.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva has attained the Great Sovereign King of the True Dharma. Throughout the three thousandfold world system, he extends the light from his white tuft of hair.
A jade vessel is filled to the brim with nectar; atop the Paṇḍaka Rock stands a vajra banner.
I prostrate to Avalokiteśvara, who has profoundly attained great mastery. With thirty-two transformation bodies, he manifests throughout the realms of the sands of the Ganges.
Therefore, the youth Sudhana dons this firm armor, able to cause auspicious radiance to surge forth from the tips of his ten fingers.
Majestic and sublime is the Honored One of Ten Thousand Virtues, standing uniquely apart from the clouds and mists.

Like the sun rising over Fusang, like the moon emerging from the vast blue sea, a single glimpse of his wondrous and sublime countenance extinguishes the sins of kalpas past; a single invocation of the Great Being’s name yields ten thousandfold merit.
Facing this radiance, body and mind naturally become peaceful and secure. Speak thus to suffering sentient beings: "Be careful not to give rise to indolence.
With compassionate vows, transform and travel through oceans of dust-mote lands; the Dharma-body rises ten thousand *yojanas* high, washing away the realms of Māras and the realms of sentient beings.
It causes the wind-circle and water-circle to tremble, and a white *puṇḍarīka* lotus boat travels through the realm of ghosts, while a blue lapis lazuli palace strikes with awe.
O Ocean Deity, may all beings together enter samādhi. Within the ambrosia flask, the willows are in full spring bloom.
Across eighty thousand *yojanas*, there is the auspicious Dharmakāya; with its thirty-two marks of response, it is the wondrous form of compassion.
Governing the lands of the ten directions, we take refuge in this one reality. Let a hundred thousand peals of thunder resound as a single dedication, as the light of the bright moon is distributed.
Amidst the myriad waters, the brocade of spring blooms upon a thousand flowers.
One should preach the Dharma with this very body, manifesting the state of youthful innocence throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Those on the cliffs gaze at the moon in the water; the moon in the water gazes at those on the cliffs.
Taking empty space as its essence and the dharma-realm as its measure, it manifests the majesty of the fourteen fearlessnesses and reveals the forms of the thirty-two marks of compassion.

The jewel in its topknot is luminous, opening the gates of liberation throughout the great trichiliocosm; the willow branch in its vase sways in the spring breeze, sweeping away the obscurations of ignorance for all sentient beings.
The warm spring sun spreads its light over clusters of a hundred flowers; the bright moon shines universally upon a thousand waves.

Hearing sounds with the eyes; using the body as the tongue. To act according to what one says, and to speak according to how one acts. A single-leaf lotus boat amidst waves and spray a thousand fathoms deep.
Of the eighty-four thousand dharma-gates of universal penetration, every hole and passage is pierced through within the pore of a lotus fiber.
He opens the gate of ambrosia and expands the ocean of compassionate vows. Seated in meditative repose upon Mount Potalaka, he attains great sovereignty.

With the water of great compassion, he nurtures the sprouts of the True Dharma; with the wind of skillful means, he causes the flowers of wisdom to bloom. He manifests the thirty-two responses and the fourteen fearlessnesses.
Every land is perfectly pervasive; every mote of dust is samādhi.

Guanyin of the Fish Basket bestows compassion upon all beings to deliver those with whom she has a karmic affinity. Her jade-like beauty is draped in lush, green clouds. At that moment, people greedily gaze at what is within her robe.
The Jewel: Thirty-six scales fly up to heaven;
a thousand catties held by a single hand. No one buys this stagnant merchandise; where is the Dragon Gate? Within the basket lies the vast blue sea.
The mute Avalokiteśvara has emerged from the fisherman’s net; brought forth, he enters the bustling basket. Seeking only to debate worth and worthlessness, he no longer avoids shame or embarrassment.
His compassionate vow is like the nurturing of spring; his heart of pity is as vast as the ocean. Do not let him be lightly leaked or betrayed—this mute one’s mouth is chattering away!
I again join my palms in reverence before the image of the Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇa with thirty-two arms;
I bow my head to this Great Being, the field of merit for this age of turbidity. Of his eighty-four thousand eyes and arms, it is only through this Great Compassion that they are manifest.
With thirty-two arms, like a great king of trees upon which all branches depend; to exhaustively examine what this symbolizes:

the forty-eight response bodies, each with one body and one arm, naturally flexing and extending; wearing Amitābha upon the crown of the head, holding the sun and moon in hand, grasping a vajra and shaking a bell.
The hosts of demons are annihilated. Grasping the blade that shaves hair, holding the four-edged tally, the wind is clear amidst the willows and the water fills the pure flask.
The arrow of diligence is set upon the bow of wisdom; the eight classes of devas and dragons gather like wind and tigers, clouds and dragons, with the lunar axe and the precious bow.

Holding a staff, spear, halberd, and戟 (ge), with the right hand in mudrā and the left in a sash; his compassion and majesty are reverent and awe-inspiring. Sometimes he binds four mudrās, or grasps two lotuses;
his great capacity responds universally, and his great function manifests before him. Sometimes he joins both palms, or clenches both fists, or extends both arms.
With his hand hanging down into the abyss, the Great Being’s single body possesses this samādhi; the eighty-four thousand [pores] are likewise so.
The great Dharma-realm is subtle enough to enter a single mote of dust; through a thousand transformations and myriad changes, all returns to the one true reality.

Zhi Zhouyu has fully mastered its subtleties; with both mind and hand forgotten, he achieves it in the space of a casual conversation. Originally, it never fell into decline; now, it likewise does not increase.
The *tāṇḍula* flower reappears; the withered tree flourishes once more. All dharmas are thus: they are free from all marks.

Like the moon in water or flowers in the sky, they are devoid of the notion of coming or going. I have composed this verse; its merit is immeasurable. It opens the gate of ambrosia and plants the banner of radiance.
At the Tiantai Jiaosi Temple in Wuxing, there was a profound spiritual resonance. A pearl from an oyster was an image of Avalokiteśvara;

bowing his head before the Great Being, he beheld the thousand billion response-bodies that arrive according to sound and respond to invocation. Within every single land and every mote of dust, all were contained within one oyster shell.
The boundless worlds are neither real nor illusory, neither vast nor narrow. It is only this pearl from the oyster, the refined essence of the sun and moon.

Who would have thought that a Great Being would be born into my family, practicing the Way in the garb of a layman, possessing such dignified and wondrous features, with a perfect pearl adorning his crown?
His radiance was immeasurable, and he was protected by the various devas. Two dragons led the way, while Sudhana paid him reverent homage.
As the kalaviṅka bird was about to sing, Master Jiang of Xunxi reflected that his hidden virtue had permeated all things; it was fitting that he should preach the Dharma with this very body.

His śarīra-skull (śakara-śiras) symbolized the Dharmakāya, embodying the Middle Way through compassionate gathering, like the springtime of the Flower Treasury World (Kusumatalagarbha). His pure jewel-like eyes symbolized Prajñā.

It illuminates and comprehends the myriad realms, leaving nothing that can escape it. The *mudrā* of the arm symbolizes liberation; through meditative concentration (*samādhi*), distraction is stilled, and all sufferings are simultaneously uprooted.
This pearl within my oyster shell is endowed with the three virtues; as emptiness, the provisional, and the middle, it is entirely subsumed within the ultimate truth.
How magnificent is Yue Xiang! Entrusted with a weight as heavy as ten thousand *jin*, he is like the *wangxiang*—formless and without intent—and yet has obtained this wish-fulfilling gem.

The Buddhas of the past and the Buddhas of the future are neither two nor different; the ocean-like wisdom of the Dharma-realm is impartial and perfectly penetrating. The pearl within the oyster of former days was a manifestation of a *arhat*.
Now, this pearl within the oyster manifests the body of the Buddha. The Buddha-body is unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) and does not fall into any numerical categories;
it is like the great void, majestically and alone revealed. Entering this pavilion, one shares the same niche with Maitreya, surrounded by ten thousand flowers—a world-transcending *udumbara* flower.
The horse-herder’s wife does not comb her hair nor wash her face; were it not for the horse-herder, how many would truly understand?
The flowing water is heartless in its longing for fallen flowers, yet for what reason do the fallen flowers follow the flowing water?
This is a painting by the scholar-official Zhao Ziyang, depicting the Great Being manifesting in the body of a civil official. Seated in tranquil repose within the Jade Hall, he preaches the Dharma.

One day, having received an imperial decree to ascend Mount Putuo, he personally beheld such a compassionate form. He vowed to produce a thousand copies to distribute among the people, for the universal benefit of all living beings.
He acted as our protector. Though the Immortal of the Jade Hall departed long ago, years beyond reckoning, this response-body remains eternally in the world.
At that time, Maoying and Taohong—sentient and insentient alike—attained Buddhahood together.
The monk Pú-dài (Baguān), the elder Qìchǐ:
little known in the monastic groves, with a protruding belly and a smiling countenance. From within his cloth bag, he brings forth one hundred and twenty items from the Tuṣita Heaven;
before the pavilions, he casts out one hundred and twenty seeds of Bodhicitta for the world of humans.
In the heavens, its traces are difficult to find. At the seventy-two marshes, the mist rises and the waters run deep.
O Ajita! Iron, Fenghua, and the tattered cloth bag demand a high price.
Taking eighty-four thousand [years] as a physical body, and taking four hundred human years as one day and night, they merely rush about from east to west, refusing to follow.

Empty and let go. The golden-colored dhūta dwells within Mount Kukkutapāda. Through many cycles of dreaming and waking, he awaits your future descent to birth, where at the three assemblies under the Dragon Flower tree, you shall speak of "zhi-hu-ye-er" (the classical particles).
With his staff he pushed open the gates of Tuṣita; with his sack he wrapped up this miserable Saṃsāra. Others have no intention to disturb the minds of sentient beings;
it is the sentient beings themselves who disturb others.
The three assemblies under the Dragon Flower tree have not yet met; through long streets and short alleys, I roam at will in feigned madness. Within this cloth bag, the universe is vast;

atop this staff, the sun and moon are long. The "dry dung pellet" of the Tuṣita Heaven and the "water-clouded village" of Vairocana’s pavilion—I claim instead that I am the true Maitreya; my family’s disgrace is needlessly broadcast abroad.
Vimalakīrti feigned illness to deceive others, yet he truly deceived himself; even the jade maidens scattering flowers knit their brows in dismay.
Had there not been the rice from the bowl of the Fragrant Accumulation, a single silence would have made it difficult to cure the hunger of the multitude.
The old man of Vaiśālī is free from dwelling or attachment; sitting alone upon his square couch, he utterly dissolves all traces of self.

Half is empty pretense, half is folly; his entire body is sickness, his entire body is medicine. When Mañjuśrī leads the assembly to engage in dialogue, at the point of ultimate realization, his mouth remains sealed.
Above, the alms-bowl’s rice is fragrant and lush; at the Dharma feast, flowers fall like rain, red and thick. This is the Āmra Grove.

In whatever place they are, the assembly shall be borne upon his palms as they return together. Before the World-Honored One, amidst hundreds of thousands of gods and men, a pure breeze shakes the sandalwood trees.
Jīvaka Mahāsattva.
I prostrate to Jīvaka, the World-transcending King of Physicians, who possesses great power of aspiration and is endowed with great majestic radiance.
For the four hundred and four maladies of sentient beings, you, Master, have eighty-four thousand remedial methods. You have two gourd vessels.
What is this wondrous medicine? It is a single root of a numinous tree that penetrates to the deepest recesses of the vital organs.

It enables all people who behold its honored image and recite its name not only to heal the chronic ailments of many lifetimes, but to directly eliminate karmic obstructions and clear away the burdens of worldly defilements, so that every pore of their body and mind attains refreshing coolness.
The Three Heads of Vajra Ucchuṣma manifest the Dharma-gate of the three contemplations; his eight arms signify the warding off of insults from the eight directions,

revealing the majestic authority of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas to rescue all sentient beings from their afflictions and sufferings— this is none other than the fire-pit of the Brahmin Jvalanānta.
This is the sword and saw of King Anala; those who hear of it hide their tracks as demons and heretics, and those who see it stand with their hair bristling in horror.
Who could be a peer to one who practices this path, upholds this dharma, manifests this form, and establishes this altar? Only Śākyamuni, the Hero of Awakening.
Avalokiteśvara and Nāgārjuna;

the Great Being Bao Gong, his mirrored countenance resplendent and his golden staff majestic. With scissors, a ruler, and a whisk, he delivered prophecies during the Qi and Liang dynasties, declaring that the Dharma would be transmitted by Bodhidharma.
The Buddha’s Mind-Seal—pursuing it, one can never catch up. It is said that after the Great Being had finished preaching the sutra, he briefly lent his majestic radiance;

throughout the day, he handled incense and selected firewood, unaware that his very body was a sacred site of practice. His wondrous form would have been difficult even for the monk Zhiwei to capture with his brush; towering and majestic, he sat alone, severing all attachments upon Dulong Peak.

The Great Being Saṃgha’s Way and Virtue was equal in its compassion; his wisdom shone universally. With his golden staff, he stabilized the ferry at the Si River, whereby demons and heretics were thereby subdued.
With a pure cloth, he contained the rain of a cascading torrent, such that not a single drop leaked through. Thus, there were thirty-six miraculous responses.
Just as the Great Being of Universal Pervasion manifested supernatural powers, his single body of adamantine density remains as imperishable as the physical body of Master Bao.
Truly, he is called the Great Sage Saṃgha Guoshi, the parent of the people throughout the nine provinces along the Long River.
The Arhat, the Worthy One, is free from afflictions. He dwells eternally among humans and does not enter nirvana. When crossing water, his heels bob up and down;
when piercing through clouds, his head is shrouded in deep blackness. He does not seek alms for himself, but desires only that sentient beings break [through ignorance].
Frugal and parsimonious, he travels across the four continents day after day. How long will it take for the stone bridge to be completed?

Facing the morning sun and the moon, through cold and heat, he wears but a single robe. He mends the old as if it were new; patching here and there, stitching horizontally and vertically. As the golden crow sinks in the west, [the work continues].
Again rising in the east, he does not take the golden needle to pass it on to others.
What matter does this single scroll of scripture discuss? It is neither the language of Tang nor the script of India.
Within the light of the jade hare, the wheel of Dharma turns; sprouts grow like the sands of the Ganges.
A needle with a hollow eye; there is no thread. Exhausting every effort, one stitches it into a single piece. How many times has the red wheel been seen to rise and fall?
Through cold and heat, this single robe is not for barter even with gold.

The Perfect and Sudden Teaching, the definitive sutras—following the lines and counting the characters, one receives them with faith and practices accordingly. This is not a partial fondness for the moon over the light;
in the secluded mountain hall, there is no lamp in the night.

At the assembly in Anāthapiṇḍada’s Garden, Subhūti questioned the Dharma as it flowed like a stream; yet at the gate of a layman’s house, he set down his bowl and departed. Seated in meditation amidst the crags, he stirred the celestial flowers;
leaning on his staff in contemplation, he found no fundamental basis upon which to rely. If one were to take emptiness and stillness as proof of perfect penetration, how could one—?
The tortoise bows its head to the Pillar of Sumeru.

Fenggan, Han, and Shishuang—these three men walk and talk of nothing but profound matters. They do not speak of Mount Emei or Mount Wutai; instead, they speak of the Western Pure Land and Guoqing Temple.
The temple’s wind and moon are shared in equal measure; beneath the cold crags, both the ugly and the clumsy are exposed. Who knows of the realm of the Great Man?
How many times have I traveled the path through the pine gate?
Hanshan and Shide: On Mount Tai in the sixth month there is snow; the world is as boiling as soup. Where the banana tree sways, the entire realm is cool and refreshing.
A single scroll of scripture in his hand—no one recognizes a single character. Barefoot he descends to Mount Emei; nine times nine is eighty-one.
In Guoqing Temple there is a man with disheveled hair; calling out to one another, they go to watch the oxen. His shorn broom and wild reeds are uniquely eccentric;
his tattered, ragged robe is all the more stylish. Picking up a single leaf of banana, he writes out a hundred pieces of "Zhang Daitou" verse.
How vexing that Fenggan lightly touched upon a taboo name, causing old Liqiu to fall into a trap to this very day.
Whoever picked this up gave it its name; yet he says, "Hanshan is my elder brother. Not allowing a single speck of dust to enter the Ultimate Reality, he entrusts all matters to his poetic sentiment.
He strikes the local deity to prevent crows from eating [the fruit], and frightens Huishan into making a tiger’s roar.
Clapping his hands and singing aloud, he departs; looking back at the cold crags, the evening clouds are level.
The iron of the Nine Provinces could not forge the single grindstone for the First Patriarch’s coming from the West; ten thousand ounces of gold could not purchase Old Xiao’s single promise.
The five-colored qilin flies up to heaven; the phoenixes of Mount Dan nest in the Aru Pavilion. A tree rises in the Eastern Land.
The Victorious Banner shakes the wooden clapper of Central India; before the Bear-Ear Peak, he swiftly turns his body. Limitless pure winds stir the vast expanse.
Ten thousand miles of waves stand still upon the Yangtze at Liang; for nine years on the ridges of Wei, the ice and snow are deep. Having cast off his entire being, he returns to the land of Chu.
The kingdom remains to this day; a single sandal weighs a thousand *qīn*.

The Fifth Patriarch sits loftily, cutting off all at White Lotus Peak; he listens in stillness as the wind whistles through the pines of ten thousand ravines. Where are the seven hundred eminent monks?
Go! In the millhouse there is rice, but no one to pound it.
Baizhang sits alone on Mount Xiong; he is a toothless tiger. Once his nose was pained, and for three days his ears were deaf. He encountered Huangbo’s obstruction.
A single slap on the cheek; pitying his child, he was unaware of its ugliness. Facing Mount Gui, he fanned the fire deep into the night, mistakenly taking orange peel for glowing embers.
He established the pure rules of the Chan garden like Xiao He codifying the laws; when he rolled up his mat before Master Ma, he was like Feng Meng shooting down Hou Yi.
His countenance was stern and formidable, difficult to approach; throughout the monasteries for a thousand ages, his majestic wind remains awe-inspiring.
The countenance of Master Linji is like the solitary fullness of the autumn moon; his virtue and realization are like the brilliant sun adorning the heavens.
He possesses a mouth capable of swallowing all Buddhas of the past, present, and future, and he is fit to clasp the shoulders of the forty-seven and twenty-three patriarchs.

Meeting the situation without yielding, he brandished the yellow cassia staff and delivered a slap across the master’s cheek; the Great Function was manifest before him. He then struck Daoyu three times under the ribs.

These four kinds of critical examination are like a tiger missing its claws or a horse lacking its fetters; the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials are like the line of Kun severing the continuity of Qian.
His descendants fill the world, all claiming to have received the Master’s direct transmission—yet they do not realize that the true...
The Dharma-Eye Treasury was extinguished and passed on to the blind donkey.
The Great Master Zhizhe of Tiantai possessed great wisdom and great eloquence; he realized the *dhāraṇī* and samādhi of the *Lotus Sūtra*'s revolving wheel—this is true essence.
Advancing, he beheld the assembly on Vulture Peak as solemnly as if it had never dispersed;

there he personally witnessed the Tathāgata preaching the *Mahā-śamatha-vipaśyanā*, raising the sun and moon of the Śakra-heaven, discoursing on the *Dhyāna-pāramitā* like the wind and thunder over the ocean of awakening, and offering the fragrant cypress of this age.

Incense coils and swirls from the golden incense burner; the moonlight enters as the curtains are drawn. One wanders upon the silver ground, gazing up at them for a thousand ages like the Great Mountains or the Northern Dipper.
For ten thousand generations they have been revered—only Nanyue and Tiantai, holding jade ruyi scepters, seated in tranquil repose upon the Vajra Terrace.
The three dots of the circular *ī* are the eye of Maheśvara; the secret treasury, layer upon layer, is entirely revealed.
Zhaozhou’s mouth was like one containing a pearl, yet his head was like a wooden ladle. In his youth he said, "I am a novice with a master," and at eighty years of age—
"Going! What a horse's hoof, what a donkey's hoof! Three or five pecks of grain; blue ash on his head; a single tusk—biting down and down.
Even if you manage to employ him throughout the twelve hours of the day, it is still nothing more than the chariots of the Qin dynasty. Tsk!"
Xuefeng’s snow covers Mount Ao; the moon shines upon Elephant Bone Peak. The iron cangue upon his neck remains undetached to this day.
Attendant Li visited Yaoshan.
Clouds in the heavens; water in a flask. To see the face is common, yet to hear the name is honored. A single stroke of such splendor cannot be painted:
from the treetops, the cold waves rise with a rustling sigh.

Pei, the State Councilor, examined the Buddha in Huangbo’s hand and the monk on the wall; with a single call of "So-and-so," he immediately bestowed a name upon him. From this, the master became his teacher and he became his disciple.
He raised his head: twelve peaks, green.
The girl Lingzhao was young, yet her sharp wit was truly praiseworthy. With a colander she fished for the white moon; with hands folded, she faced Danxia.
Together they spoke of the discourse on non-arising; do not spread the hemp upon the tree. At the moment of death, she looked at the color of the sun—she has deceived the old patriarch to his death.
In the waters and mountains of Huangniu Lake, one finds much delight; yet boundless wind and moon fade away in darkness. Upon the horn of the yellow ox lies a scroll of verse;
half is the song of the woodcutter, half the song of the herdsman.
Master Yushan has traveled through Chaling for many years; How many times have spring rains and spring clouds gathered?
Had it not been for that somersault on the donkey’s back, The bright pearl would have been lost, with no place to find it.

Lan Zan dwells where the mountain peaks are shrouded in deep clouds and the paths are cut off; he spends his life lying beneath the wisteria vines. For ten years the Chancellor has been too light in his talk;
now this one eminent monk enjoys the reputation of "The Lazy One. When the imperial summons suddenly arrived from the heavens, the price of yam tubers was raised from that point on.
Liancheng: "Who nowadays possesses such a bearing? Let us see how many times the Yellow River will clear again.
Master Jingtian Tong, the two white oxen have their eyebrows standing upright; the three-faced cat has its nostrils sunken. A single leather boot is capable of scraping [the ground]."
Liberation! When the moon is bright, the golden phoenix dwells in the dragon’s nest.
Chan Master Yuanjue Yan of Xuefeng was proficient in both principle and expression;
he moved with unimpeded mastery in all directions. He kicked over Mount Sumeru and trampled the ocean of perfect enlightenment, thereby attaining the Original Source.

The profound and secret intent is fully understood as the tongs and hammer that transform delusion into awakening; it is like rolling a wooden ball down a snowy peak, intended to reveal the furnace and bellows that refine the ordinary into the sacred.
Standing alone with feet planted firm before a precipice ten thousand fathoms high, one touches the nostrils of the ancestral style.

Upon the crossroads, there is a broken tile; the skull is ever-dry within the world. Shining through antiquity and surging through the present, its radiance is magnificent and vast. This indeed is it.
This is what is called the "heavenly robe and heavenly bowl"—the direct descendants. To try to see him at Wangzhou Pavilion or Wushan Ridge is much like being a lacquered bucket;
it is not satisfactory. *Duḥ!* (A shout of exasperation)

When the late master Yuexi Heshang (who succeeded Chijue) shaved my head, he employed the "blinding the eyes" method and unleashed a thunderbolt-like mechanism; he scraped the frost from my face while his breast was utterly devoid of compassion.
Severing the flow of the Luo River, fish and dragons beg for their lives; releasing the tiger of the South Mountain, the lion conceals its majesty.
Seated upon the four sites of enlightenment, he wields the true command; with a bald brush held upside down, he paints the brows of the goddesses.
Master Gutian Zituo carries the official mold to break up Tianran’s household; he employs the severed rope to pierce the nostrils of the patch-robed monks.
He releases the featherless iron falcon to test the dragons and snakes of the four seas. Having no desire to become a Buddha or an Ancestor, he makes his living with the hoe as circumstances allow.
This is what is called being outside the Baiyun Pass.

Emerging from the ridges, he was the Dharma heir of the Venerable Xuansha, Yuyang, and Hengchuan, and the bone-grandson of Songyuan. He extinguished the orthodox eye of the Linji school and shattered the [lineage] of Zhongfeng.
A sand basin. He lost his sword in the Kunming Pool, yet he retrieved his saw from the banks of the Qujiang River. It soars through the present and shines upon antiquity;
it shakes the heavens and stirs the earth. The Yellow River flows in nine bends, its waters emerging from Kunlun.

The celestial omen of our late master, Venerable Huyan, was such that the pearls of the dragon could be plucked and his tiger whiskers could be stroked; yet he remained a formidable figure, inviolable and majestic, whose commands were enforced throughout Wuyue.

Venerable Zhuxi of Tiantong possessed eyes like those of a river and a mouth like a sea; his mind was as fine as brocade and his inner being as embroidered with thread. His vast capacity swallowed the Taihu Lake, and his brilliant radiance shone like the light of Mount Taibai.
When he rebuked and scolded, he encompassed all with the springtime’s nurturing; when he showed compassion, he was as stern as the midday sun or autumn frost. He brought forth the profound...
The words of Sha-wei have not yet been fully realized. Like Zhenjing’s verification of Jiyin’s gold, refined a hundred times;
or like picking up Dongshan’s three blows of the staff, which resembles Ciming’s release of the fragrance of nine-transformed cinnabar from Jicui.
Transverse and vast, formidable and majestic—this is what is called the fifth generation of Mount Zhongfeng, providing the cool shade of a great tree.
Venerable Huiji of Mount Jing: his countenance was like that of the emaciated Mahāmati;
his wit and intelligence possessed the eloquence of Yongming. Like the National Teacher, he let out a thunderous roar;

with four whips, he struck like falling stars and flashing lightning. Grasping the literary brush of the Vimalakīrti Chamber, he could lift nine *zhe* of weight; he was a great general who established [the Dharma].

When the banners and drums sound, the three armies grow faint with fear of battle; yet this stone chamber is that which overcomes the household. It is sufficient to join the fragrant blossoms and continue the blazing flame.
Countless pine flowers and a thousand fathoms of snow-white silk remain hanging even now before the Milk Peak; those who come shall each behold the skillful means therein.
Venerable Master Tianmu Zhongfeng was a model for Buddhas and patriarchs and a paragon for devas and humans. His capacity was as deep as the ocean; his speech and silence were as vibrant as spring.
He shattered coral against his iron whip and scattered true pearls across his silk curtains. He regarded the body as an illusion and dwelt within illusion as the body;
he saw that marks are identical to reality, and that total reality is devoid of marks. Praised and extolled, he was titled National Teacher Puying.
Gazed upon and revered, he was originally Master Zhongfeng.

Chan Master Dajian Deng, a venerable elder dwelling in meditation, is an old blind shaveling. In his conduct and concealment, he does not prize cleverness or slowness; in his employment and relinquishment, he seeks only the clumsy and the swift.

He is like the Old Barbarian (Bodhidharma) who stepped upon the whale-waves; he resembles Kāśyapa returning to Kukkuṭapāda Mountain after his samādhi. Like Mount Jufu and Mount Jinbao, he acts in accordance with his nature.
Abbot: At Mount Ruilong and Mount Ruelu, you remain entirely free from constraints; watching the boat races at the head of the Zhuojin River, you do not fail as the National Teacher of Nanyang.
Playing with monkeys on the Tianjin Bridge, you excel at circulating the "poisonous charm" of the Yongyuan lineage.
The bright lamp of Lingfeng illuminates the night; a broken string must be mended with *luan* glue.
The Way of National Teacher Mujaku of Kōmyō Peak is as heavy as a mountain;
his mind is as clear as the moon. His eyes fix upon the five Sumeru mountains; his mouth swallows the Buddhas of the three periods of time.

He strikes the yellow sand of his almsbowl until it rings with a golden sound; the roots of his aged vegetables are sweeter than cliff-honey. When the wild sheep hang by their horns, they leave no trace—ten thousand [miles].
The ancient Flower Peak rises high and imposing;

Tianyi Duanjiang, an eighty-year-old patriarch of Chan, has cleared the eyes of the four seas. His face bears the ancient hue of Mount Kuanglu, and his body is like a singular peak shaped like a standing brush.
Hearing his proclamations, Fuyou would surely nod in agreement; observing his origins, how could Damei have been of a different spirit?
Like a wild goose passing through the vast sky, its reflection sinks into the cold waters.

Continuing the ancestral tradition of the furnace and bellows that smelt gold, like the autumn moon and the midnight bell on a frosty night, I shall see the Way of this Hermitage shine with great brilliance and extend far and wide.
It is inexhaustible.
The Preface and Seven Eulogies by Xu Daqing:
The Daoist of Yùqīng Guàn in Yúnjiān, the Dharma Master Jìngjì, Xu Daguan, has applied his mind to our Great Sage.
His dedication to the Way was profound. He personally transcribed the entire *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* three times; the complete *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* forty-six times;
and the *Śūraṅgama Samādhi Sūtra*, the *Amitāyurdhyāna Sūtra*, and other scriptures beyond counting. Furthermore, he constructed two stupas for the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.

He constantly maintained the *Cundī Dhāraṇī* and practiced the cultivation of purity and tranquility, as well as the transformation [of others]. When his disciples followed his final instructions regarding his funeral pyre, they obtained his uncorrupted remains.
There are six [relics]: the finger joints, the crown of the head, the teeth, the tongue, the prayer beads, and the bone of the right knee.

There are two auspicious omens: the *śarīra* (relics) and the transformed Buddha images. His disciple, Dharma Master Xuansu and Cao Shiqin, because their master had formerly traveled with me, requested that I write an inscription for them so that they might be believed in future generations. Thus, I have composed a eulogy for each, saying: [The eulogies follow.]
When the finger joints are spread, they form a palm; when joined, they form a fist. Within the tip of a single hair, one can compress the great trichiliocosm;

by breaking open a single atom, one brings forth a vast scripture. One may dip the brush into the vast ocean and write without ever tiring. For this reason, the ten fingers constantly radiate precious light.
Amidst the blazing flames, he stands resplendent and firm; honored above and below, he points to heaven and points to earth.
This Dharma Master of mine is likewise so.
He wore a precious crown upon his head, resembling that of the Great Bodhisattva. After the cremation, his remains were solid and resplendent; the *śarīra* relics were innumerable.

One such relic rested upon the crown of his head, brilliant and magnificent, as precious as pearls and jade, and as radiant as *gui* and *zhang* ceremonial vessels. From the crown of his head to his heels, and from his heels back to the crown of his head, [the relics were distributed].
This is the banner of diligence; this is the great round mirror. The conch-like hair is unburnt, and the crest-jewel is ever-luminous.
Therefore, when this skull is struck, it produces the sound of gold.
The hymns of praise for the Buddha Vehicle all issue from his mouth; therefore, his teeth and gums remain indestructible even after cremation.

When the World-Honored One was cremated, Śakra rained down flowers and dispatched two swift messengers to steal his precious teeth. How could it be otherwise? For the Dharma Master embodies loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity.
These are his teeth; no one dares to steal them. The dark pearls are crystalline and bright, set upon his withered gums. Encased in gold and jade, they are displayed to the people of the world.

The tongue is the sixth faculty of experience. Examining its merits, it is solely through the power of the tongue that one thousand and two hundred subtle and wondrous Dharma gates are proclaimed on behalf of the Buddha.
Therefore, the root of this tongue emits the fragrance of a lotus flower; it acts according to what it speaks, and speaks according to what it acts.

The fire is cold and the ashes are frigid, like the crescent moon at its first appearance. One thoroughly understands that the nature of taste is neither existent nor empty; thus the Medicine Kings Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata together realize perfect penetration.

Reciting the name of the Buddha with a rosary, one does not forget Him day or night. The hundred and eight mani jewels reflect one another like the interlacing light of Indra’s net; within that radiance, one serves all Buddhas.
Like a tile used for knocking at a door, or a raft for crossing a river, the beads are themselves the Buddha, and the Buddha is himself the beads.

When the fuel is exhausted, the fire is extinguished; the essence of the jewel remains as it is (tathatā). Like a firm and solid banner, donning the armor of patience, even when the three calamities pervade all, this jewel remains ever-present.

With the right knee bone, one gazes upon and pays homage to the Holy Countenance. With each prostration and each kneel, every single atom [of this knee] attains the rank of a Universal Monarch (*cakravartin*).

In its bending, stretching, bowing, and rising, it encounters the source of truth on both left and right. For this reason, when this knee enters fire, it is not consumed. One falls by means of the knee; one rises by means of the knee.

He breaks the banner of arrogance and performs reverent repentance. The spirit of the valley does not die; the Mysterious Female endures forever. May the auspicious response of the numinous *lingzhi* bring blessings upon his descendants.
The physical body of the Śarīra ultimately returns to decay; yet within that decay, its radiance is magnificent. The rite of cremation originated in Zhugan (India);
the *śarīras* were brilliantly manifested in eighty-four thousand pieces. Precepts can give rise to meditative concentration, and meditative concentration can give rise to wisdom.

Jade-like in its luster, mountains shine with its brilliance; pearls are bright, and rivers are made beautiful by it. With no Maitreya behind and no Śākyamuni before, there is only this Bodhisattva—a lotus flower blooming amidst the flames.
Among those of the lineage of the immortal-seekers who transform themselves into Buddha-images, they dwell in tranquil seclusion. There, a manifested Tathāgata appears upon their crowns.

Texts such as the *Śūraṅgama-samādhi*, the *Amitāyurdhyāna*, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, and the *Avataṃsaka* circulate and are transcribed by them in numbers like the sands of the Ganges; stupas of Prabhūtaratna emerge from the tips of their pens.
He divided his seat to discourse on the sutras; this was the transformation Buddha. He threw himself into a mass of fire to open the gate of the supreme heat. All things are of one body;
heaven and earth share the same root.
Regarding my own praise:
Elder Ching-chueh T’eng of Chen-ching Monastery invited me to Chen-ching;
there was a great karmic affinity. His faith was so sincere that he fulfilled the perfection of giving, spreading gold to establish a Jetavana Grove, emulating the deeds of Master Nan-yang.
Accumulated Green: Looking up toward the Cloud Gate of Wondrous Joy (Miaoxi), I can only feel that my realization falls short of the ancient masters and am ashamed before the former sages.

Fortunately, there are the master and disciple of Chicken Peak; how could this hinder the continuation of the flame and the succession of the fragrant lineage? From now on, the ancestral estate of Caoxi shall flourish, and its legacy may be passed down through descendants for a thousand years.

The Elder Tang of Yanfeng in Fuzhou requested [this] like the azure of gathering clouds and the clarity of settled silt. Even Shisong Kuang could not match his keen hearing; how could Li Lou rival his vision?
Amidst the golden hue within ten thousand smelting furnaces and the sound of the stream upon a hundred-fold rapids—this is what I expect of you.
When there is flight that pierces the heavens, there is a cry that startles the world.
Elder Dàyún Mǎn invited nine-nines and ten-tens;
though he has many years, he lacks virtue. A broken sand bowl is worth more than a city of jade, while the pearl from the dragon’s jaw is not worth a single coin.
Not straightforward. If one lets go, great clouds bring a soaking rain; if one holds fast, the empty chamber becomes bright white. From where does the rain come? What color is the wind?
When the peach blossoms bloom and the waves warm, the Dragon Gate opens; amidst the bright sun and blue sky, thunder and lightning crash.

The Elder of Pukinji requested the striking of the phoenix-robe and dragon-drum; he sought salt to offer to the horse. The kalpa-stone may be worn away, yet the sound of the pines in the wind is priceless. This is entrusted to Pukinji.
Dae-haeng delivered this discourse.

The elder Seong-san Sin invited Na-eok Song-chang, whose nature was as defiant as frost-kissed chrysanthemums and whose yellow hue was like that of autumn. His power of concentration was as firm as a mountain fortress, and his stubborn character was like tempered metal and stone.
This is the firmness [of the Way]. Using the seven-pierced, eight-perforated pine-root broom of Songyuan, he sings the "Song of Deceptive Emptiness" of Zhongfeng;
shifting keys and changing melodies, the moon spreads its reflection across a thousand rivers, and the lamp divides its light into infinite beams.
There is one whose mind is empty like a mirror who plants my high banner of Tian Rui.
The Elder Daoji Zhong requests his retirement; old and decrepit, he is dazed and deluded. Mount Sumeru rests comfortably in his nostrils; with a bald broom, he paints the蛾眉 (mei) eyebrows.

Sitting at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, he loathes being a Buddha. For a lifetime he has carried a single wooden board, yet there is no place to thrust a needle. The river moon shines upon the pines.
The wind blows. To walk this path and save these times—one must be a lion cub who returns to defeat the enemy.
Elder Guī of Mingyin in Taizhou requested:
"A mere lacquer bucket! Utterly devoid of nostrils! Grasping the authentic tongs and hammer, he drives a nail through the single seam of empty space.
This is neither Huangbo’s great capacity nor Xuefeng’s great function. Like the resonance of jade and the sound of metal, like the wind blowing and the thunder rolling:
from the tip of the staff he strikes out the Jade Qilin; from the crown of the head he releases the Phoenix of the Cinnabar Mountain.
Attendant Ditan Huan requested that the Great River be laid out in full breadth. Old banyan trees cover the courtyard; South Peak stands like a barrier, and North Ridge like a screen.

Here grows this nameless weed, neither a hero among men nor blessed by the spirit of the land. Even the ancient pines and massive rocks cannot compare to its longevity; the mountain stream flows on through autumn.

The moon—nothing can serve as a metaphor for its purity. To magnify his illustrious lineage, which is like the *utpala* flower, is like the brilliant light of the eastern sky. At the request of the attendant Master Yuanda, [The text continues...

A gentle breeze blows through the secluded pines; a cool moon hangs in the azure void. Forgetting both mind and environment, I sit in tranquil meditation upon the flat stone.
I do not secretly scatter true pearls within the purple silk curtains, nor do I idly cast away tiles and rubble at the gate of the bustling market.
This is the person who has attained the Way through non-action; with a single phrase of clear realization, they transcend billions of worlds.

The Master Guanzhu invited [the assembly] to contemplate the true mark of the body; the contemplation of the Buddha is likewise so. That contemplator of illusions remains steadfast through successive kalpas. Within the Hall of Jasper Seating, he leisurely grasps the fly-whisk;
atop the Tower of Pure Breeze, he strikes the lion-stringed lute. He is the successor to the orthodox lineage of the Eastern Mountain of Prajñā. Free from...
The transmission of Kungo Chungfeng: when the bell is suspended in its frame, it resonates with every strike; when the mirror faces its stand, who is ugly and who is beautiful?
The bowl of Shaolin rings with a sound like gold and jade; the lamp of Caoxi continues its flame in a fragrant succession.

The Abbot Lin, with his head white and teeth yellow, possesses not an inch of talent. He feels shame at Śākyamuni’s preaching of the sudden and the gradual, and laughs at Bodhidharma’s travels through Wei and Liang.
He revives the lingering echoes of the sand-basin from Mount Zhongfeng and brings forth the brilliant radiance of the Tianrui lineage across generations. It is like striking—
Like polished jade and resonant bells, where among the green mountains is there not a site for practice?

At the request of the attendant Shousong and the head of the monastery, we traveled six or seven li into the mountains. Holding my staff in hand, I felt weary as I grew old and reluctant to ascend the heights; every ten steps, I paused nine times.
The wind of heaven cools my breast; the moon upon the pines illuminates my heart. Guarding the truth and concealing my clumsiness, I stand upon Mount Song and lie upon Mount Shaoshi.
One flower and five petals—how fragrant they flow! This true and wondrous secret was not transmitted from father to son.

The Elder Tiantai Zifu De requested that my response be straightforward rather than ornate, and simple rather than self-conceited. At times it is adorned with the myriad virtues; at other times, the Buddha’s face appears as a hundred deformities.
Atop a solitary peak, he roars at the moon and sleeps amidst the clouds; on the crossroads of the city street, he points at the hawthorn tree and scolds the willow.
Casting aside the wooden ladle that serves thousands and hundreds of myriads, he opens his mouth to swallow all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
The single broken sand-pot of the Patriarch is called the measureless peck of Caoxi; he hands it all at once over to the solitary cloud, who heads toward Mount Tiantai.
In the midst, he let out a great lion’s roar.
Like Yue the Vinaya Master, he invited the pupils;
his ears were deaf, yet his hearing surpassed that of Li Lou. [He was] the Moon at Stone Bridge, the Pine on the Min Peaks. The pine grows long.
Azure. The moon travels through the sky; this is what is called the Elder Pines-and-Moon.
At the request of the steward De-luk, he resided at Jiu-feng Guanyin Chan Monastery in Wenzhou.
A tree has its root; water has its source. From the sprouting of shoots to the formation of cross-grained knots and coiled roots, and from the initial contact with the flood to—
The waters submerge the sun and flood the heavens; how could such a being have any concern for responding to the world, nor any intention to wield power?

To obtain its blessings and longevity is but a minor fruit of the human and celestial realms. It possesses both its essence and its function, yet it is not something that can be transmitted from father to son.
A broken sandpot, struck here and there; a broom-handle with seven holes and eight piercings. Who would have known that the True Dharma Eye was extinguished upon a blind donkey?
At the request of the Elder Zhong of Renwang Monastery in Huzhou.
Mazu’s single shout left Baizhang deaf; Muzhou’s single squeeze broke Yunmen’s leg.
There are clouds and billows reaching the heavens that can accommodate fish that swallow ships; there are wind-circles sustaining the world that can carry wings that scrape the sky.
When the Great Function manifests, it abides by no fixed rules. Beneath the golden incense burner lies Kunlun; within the Pishai Lake...
The bright moon is bestowed in its entirety upon the Benevolent King. To forge a sword, one must use the iron of Binzhou.
Elder Jian of Pingjiang Taiping requests:
"When body and mind are as one, there is nothing remaining outside the self. At the tips of the hundred grasses, who is named Maitreya? Within the village of three families..."
The Non-dual Mañjuśrī sometimes points to the seventy-two peaks of Dongting Lake, transforming them into pure gold and fine jade;
at other times, he churns the thirty-six thousand acres of Lake Tai, turning it all into *amṛta* (clarified butter). In the Great Peace, there is originally no form;
why needlessly apply such superficial coatings? Wine has always been delicious without resorting to back alleys; vinegar is not found in large gourds.
Elder An of Huirui Monastery at Yanshan requested:
"The mind is like cold ashes; speech is like withered wood. It is as level as a mirror’s surface, yet as precipitous as a hanging cliff.
Having bitten through Dongshan’s iron sour pastry, all manner of rare delicacies are simultaneously complete. Picking up Xuefeng’s wooden ladle, fifteen hundred..."

A hundred people all scoop it up and bring it here; the Beneficent Sun shines with renewed brilliance, and one might halt its course by brandishing a halberd. Once the wild waves have overturned, the Pillar of砥 (Dizhu) can turn them back.
At the peak of Yandang, the sun stands at its zenith; staffs fall like raindrops and shouts roar like thunder.
The Elder Miaoxiangzong of Xuanzhou invites [the assembly]:
"The clouds hang across the Jade Bench; the waters of Caoxi are clear. The source of the mind is profound and still; the wondrous marks are perfectly luminous.

Employing the broom-handle of Songyuan, he causes his commands to be carried out throughout Wu and Yue; raising the broken sand-pot of Zhongfeng, its value exceeds that of a city. Having such a father, there must necessarily be...

Having obtained such a son, one will surely obtain his emolument and his fame. Acting as he speaks, and speaking as he acts, he shall cause our celestial auspiciousness—the fundamental principle of the tradition—to resound like jade and ring like metal.

Elder Chan of Fahu Monastery in Wenzhou requested that Chan manifest great potential and display great function. He cast forth Linji’s Three Essentials and Three Mysteries and seized hold of Fenyang’s Seven Captures and Seven Releases.
Like a bell suspended on its frame—struck with great force, it rings out loud; like an arrow leaving the bowstring—shot a hundred times, it hits the mark every time. Yongjia...
Overnight he headed for Caoxi; on his shoulders rested the great Dharma, heavy as a thousand-jin weight.
At the request of Elder Jinxian of Chuzhou Jinxian Temple, the ancient Buddha emitted light. As the time had arrived, the brilliance was fully manifested. He raised the stone axe.
The Axe: Having attained the Great Pivot, he manifested the Great Function; he burned Huangbo’s meditation board to settle the fundamental tenet and establish the Dharma banner.
If only one can make the tip of the staff as bright as the sun, there will be no need for Linji’s "understanding and taking charge."
The Elder Yanfeng of Fuzhou invites [you to see that] the eyes arise from the three corners;
the head is as steep as the Five Peaks. Throughout the entire Great Canon of the Teachings, one expounds and enters into them—whom can it be said is without words?

Throughout the trichiliocosm of sand-grain worlds, they are cast away and tossed back; taking error for right, from the moment one hears the sound of Yanxi’s stream, the qilin snaps its golden tether.
Letting go of West Monastery’s wooden snake and picking up Master Zeng’s wooden ladle—this is what is called the awakened one awakening those yet to awaken.
At Mount Moshan in Fuzhou, Elder Hui invited Wisdom as his bow and Diligence as his arrow.
Moving freely in every direction—seven strides and eight turns—he manifested ten thousand transformations and a thousand changes. He was like a great bell suspended from its frame:
struck with force, it rings out loud; struck gently, it rings softly. He was like a bright mirror set upon a stand: when a Hu comes, he appears as a Hu; when a Han comes, he appears as a Han.
On the summit of Mount Matsu, he radiates rays from his brow; amidst the sound of thunder, lightning flashes forth. Mirroring the earth and illuminating the heavens—Sun Face, Moon Face.
At the request of the Elder Kaja of Sekizan in Fukujō.
A spring flows from within the rock; this is the source of awakening. The moon hangs amidst the pines, its light penetrating the great trichiliocosm.
The Great Image at Jia Prefecture does not touch the ground with its heels; the Iron Ox of Shan Prefecture has nostrils that reach up to the heavens.
Dream-like shadows arise and perish through beginning and end, yet the pure *dharmakāya* remains eternally firm throughout kalpas. One’s entire life is found at the edge of the mattock.

At the request of the Elder Chanxiang Zhen of Jiangyin, [I] praise the one who is as snow-proud and pine-green, whose chrysanthemums are yellowed by the frost; who occupies the precious lotus throne of the Universal Monarch upon the jade desk; who plants the celestial banner of radiant victory;
who treads the ground of the reality-limit of True Suchness; who delights in the fragrance of dhyāna-joy and the bliss of Dharma; and who roars like a lion.
The vermilion phoenix soars aloft; great function and great capacity manifest as auspicious omens and blessings. A single flower of the udumbara blooms, its fragrance pervading all realms.
Attendant Xing of Raoyou requests:
where person and environment are one, and form and emptiness are unimpeded, there is but the single, adamantine body that does not oppose the various sensory objects.
Passing the imperial examination? Let them pass as they please. Standing out from the crowd? Let others excel as they will. Three thousand miles away there is one who understands;
at the corner of the house, the pines and wind play the celestial music.

Peak Head Seat invites the enemy of Buddhas and Patriarchs, the pestilence of the monastic groves. The Eye of the True Dharma was extinguished by a blind donkey; for forty years he has stirred up dust and soil.
A single phrase cuts through like a chisel striking iron. Peculiar, indeed! At the solitary peak of Wondrous Summit, the clouds; at the stream of Caoxi, the stream.
Last month,
the Abbot Xuan invited that which is the most wondrous among wonders and the most profound among profundities: galloping horses at the bottom of the great ocean, and sailing ships atop Mount Sumeru.
The mani-jewel is entrusted to both hands; the *liji* thorn is swallowed at will. The iron whip shatters the coral tree;
the moon is full upon the branches of the Fusang tree.
Quick-witted attendants, people’s faculties vary—some sharp, some dull. The Way has no North or South Lineage. To the swift and brilliant monk, it is entrusted directly with both hands.
The golden circle has its seven holes and eight openings; the chestnut burr is swallowed from the east and spat out from the west. It requires one to accept it immediately and directly. Cao.
The Dharma of Master Xixi is not so extensive. Custodian Mao has requested [this teaching]:
"The countenance is loathsome and the words lack flavor. Cast aside this man from Muzhou who carries a single board and sees only one side; lift it up!
When Yunmen brought forth "a dried-up shit-stick," it was entirely devoid of breath; yet to turn the entire Great Canon with a single breath is not yet to be a true master.
To turn the Wheel of Dharma thrice throughout the great universe, leaving no room for deliberation—how magnificent is that achievement! My Way has gone East.
The tree rises up with radiant light like a banner of victory; boundless pure winds stir heaven and earth.
The attendant Qing invites silence, forgetting words; still yet ever-illuminating, it is like the moon reflected in a thousand rivers, or like the wind whistling through ten thousand hollows.
The mind requires no investigation; it is like Ānanda’s vast learning. The flower has never been plucked, yet it evokes the smile of Kāśyapa.

Utterly transcending the sense bases and their objects, the numinous light shines alone. Amidst a thicket of a hundred flowers appears the udumbara; from within the golden-furred cave comes the lion’s roar.
The Abbot of Zhenjing Faming Monastery invites [the assembly]:
The pines are verdant and vast; the moon is bright and clear. Grasp this wondrous luminosity of Zhenjing, and it shall shatter delusive thoughts and inverted views.
Sometimes he takes up a single blade of grass and makes it the sixteen-foot golden body; sometimes he takes that sixteen-foot golden body and makes it a single blade of grass.
He takes a bowl of rice from the zenith to receive those coming from all directions; with half a drop of water from Caoxi, he universally nourishes the withered and parched.
For a thousand ages, his descendants have looked up to his pure bearing; in the grove of coral trees, the sun shines bright and clear.
The lay nephew Liu Qiu has not been at home for over fifty years;
he clenches his two fists and makes his own living. Within the garden of Master Liu, there are a thousand peach trees;
as spring goes and comes, how many times have the flowers bloomed? Painted in colors, they are neither form nor non-form; hung out in the open, they face the sun.
Is it real? Is it false? Now I sing a tune of returning home; no one beneath my eyes can recognize him.
I tell you: this is the Son of the Pengcheng Clan, who at thirteen years of age became a monk.
He has eaten how much of the monastery’s rice and tea!
The head seat Pujue requested:
"To establish all phenomena from the ground of non-abiding—once one enters the realm of words and ink, it immediately becomes false and illusory. At the bottom of the great ocean..."
Stirring up dust and raising clouds of soil; on the summit of Mount Sumeru, waves surge and billows rise. In Huai Prefecture, the ox eats the grain; in Yi Prefecture, the horse’s belly swells.
From of old, the subtle essence has never been transmitted from father to son; the radiance of the sword pierces straight through to the Ox and Dipper constellations above.
The attendant Siding, a successor of the lamp, requested:
"To turn one's back on the edge of the sword; to gallop across the surface of ice. A solitary valley, the ancient orthodox lineage of Dongshan; the true essence of the Linzhin anvil, a monk from Min.
There is no dharma to be transmitted; the lamp continues as an inexhaustible light. Fatherly kindness and filial piety; the moon is white."
The river is clear; he seizes the lightning-flash to serve as a torch, yet returns at noon to strike the third watch.
Attendant Daohong asked, "Is the Way far?
[Dongshan replied: "It is true in every encounter. "A person can broaden the Way; it is not the Way that broadens the person. At the tip of a single hair—
Manifesting the Jewel King realm, sitting within a mote of dust, he turns the Great Dharma Wheel; in the lion’s den there are no other beasts, for from an iron ox is born a jade qilin.
Verses by the Disciple Zhicheng, Compiled in Homage to the Fourth Patriarch,
the Living Body of the Great Physician.
Majestically seated, he cuts off Mount Pòtóu; throughout the entire world, his bare flesh-ball is impossible to conceal. A tiger to the right, a dragon to the left—the green is not yet finished;
a single branch protrudes askew, utterly without cause.
I bow to the five patriarchs;
Great Man’s flesh-body has emerged once more, yet affairs are already many. His surname was not ordinary—how could it be otherwise? The single session at Huangmei remains even now:
the nine apertures and hundred bones are but an anthill.
I pay homage at the Stupa of Master Bao;
the hungry hawk’s talons are blunt, yet the mirror reflects my shameful countenance. The nest is cold, unable to withstand the wind at the treetops.
Since falling into the net of Qi and Liang, there has been no way to escape the cage until this day.
Following the ten verses of Master Gulin that modeled those of Fenyang to distinguish the correct from the deviant, there were as many seekers as hemp stalks at every door.
Those who came must be taught to verify right and wrong; it is like seizing a tiger amidst a flash of lightning.
The rhinoceros. Within a flash of lightning, distinguish the dragon from the snake;
do not let your confusion obscure True Suchness, nor remain muddled and vague. Do not let your ignorance obscure Buddha-nature; when the Great Spirit raises his hand, there is no more to it.
My son, you have shattered the thousandfold Great Flower Mountain.

Your skillful discernment reveals that the eight returns are not real; your investigation of the source of seeing proves it is fundamentally not delusion. Your seven-point inquiry into the mind exposes the error of mistaking the false for the true. How could my grace not bestow upon you samādhi?
Power! Ānanda speaks of his own celestial kin in vain;
he may occupy the Lion’s Seat in full before the western river, yet if one intends to deliberate with him, it will cause his soul to lose its courage. A single sheet of paper-money and some wine.
Flesh! Idle gods and wild ghosts compete to rush toward it;
it is like what was sought at Mount Jing—what was obtained was no fine jade—and what was sought at the Red Water—what was found was not a pearl. It is best to strike them all down with a single blow.
Shattered! The bearded monk from the Western Heaven has no whiskers.

Discerning the master’s [action] is like a clap of thunder shaking the earth, impossible to evade; the blazing sun shines upon the great thousandfold world. When swordsmen meet, there is no other way.
Matter: Grinding and polishing the three-footed ancient Longquan sword;

recognizing the pivot of the encounter, where beneath Deshan’s staff, life and death are complete; within Linji’s shout, host and guest are distinguished. To hesitate for even a moment is like ten thousand miles of white clouds.
Li. At Lantian, he was suspected of killing General Li.
Within these lines, the true meaning is revealed:
"When Dangyang breaks out, it is a浑侗 (hún lón) line. Press down on the cloud-head and examine it closely. The legless immortal splits open his chest.
A kick! The Silent Boy’s mouth chatters on.

Xianzong employs the principle that both teaching and realization are pervasive, with essence and function fully integrated. He hurls forth the thorny briar and the golden circle; see if you can swallow them through. You cannot.
In vain, you act as a direct descendant of Yangqi;
few know the Master’s skillful means of "plucking from the white. The old rishi has hair growing on his teeth; when have his limbs ever been borrowed from without?
Verse: Holding up a bald broom upside down to paint the蛾眉 (eyebrows);
In sum, this praises the monk who must penetrate the patriarch’s mechanism. The Great Way stands majestic, reaching the nine thoroughfares; The Ten Sages and Three Worthies clarify this.

The Essential Meaning: The myriad phenomena of the universe revolve around the pivot of spiritual wisdom. He snatches the ceremonial tablet from the hands of the stone statue and plucks the pearl from beneath the jaw of the black dragon.
Having utterly defeated both the Duke of Fenyang and the floating Buddha, he transforms the fish that scale the three tiers of the Dragon Gate.
Sending off the monk to pay homage at Wutai:
within the gathered radiance of his body, the golden bridge appears; amidst the lion’s roar, the jade arm extends.
Having thoroughly scrutinized the old woman of Mount Tai, who else could there be after Zhaozhou?
Entrusted to my Chan friend:
The vast ocean is windless, yet its waves strike the heavens; within its depths, the fields of mulberry trees appear again and again.
Asuras gather flowers to brew wine, until even Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra fall prostrate in intoxication.
Seeing off the Head Seat Cheng as he pays homage to the Patriarchs:
Green mountains are countless, waters are boundless. The moon is full where the mist of Xiang shrouds it. A fall need not require another prostration;
the nostrils of the Patriarchs are pierced all at once.
Presented to the Guest of Lingyan Temple:

The inkstone pool is fragrant with spring water and fine tea is freshly brewed. As the sound of footsteps echoes through the corridor, guests gaze upon one another. We shall idly offer the courtyard cypress as a subject for pure conversation;
behind the screen, there is now no longer the Great Master Han.
Next, following the rhyme of Chief Prosecutor Gwan-jeom, I lament the passing of Master Go-rim:
the phoenix has flown and the terrace is empty; the virtuous grieve. The Dharma-body alone is revealed, utterly without dependence. Beneath the Vajra Banner, a pure breeze rises;
of those who listen to this song of non-arising, there are few.
From antiquity to the present, a single yawn; across the vast ocean of kalpas, clouds of dust arise.
Last night, space performed a somersault, startling those gathered on the Vulture Peak.
Presented to the portrait of Shen Yueyan:

A single skin-bag is originally a delusion; to add another is to increase the delusions even more. The moon over a thousand rivers and the moon over a thousand cliffs—before the brush, the immortal has no recourse.
I visited Master Gaseppo but did not meet him;
he does not dwell at Nanhu, but resides at Donghu. A master craftsman of this age who remains unpatterned even in old age—where did his small boat moor last night?
The clear waves coldly reflect the solitary orb of the moon.

Inscription for the Hall of Cultivating Seclusion Chang Ju and Jie Ni: grain grows upon the ridges; Jing Li and Dong Yuan: mushrooms fill the fields. Beneath the hall, a single plow has been well-served by the fresh rain;
In the spring breeze, the water-buffalo is too weary to be spurred further.
Seeing off the Venerable Taivina as he returns to Wanshou to visit his teacher:
The autumn wind rises over the white artemisia in the sea country; Roll up your robes and return home—do not linger. The Master is old and his heart is deeply lonely;
He needs someone right now to rub his back.
To Zen practitioner Biao:
The river wind is piercing, the snow falls thick and white. You have come to my door to inquire about the silent void. It is best to hear my name and leave without meeting me;
in old age, I lack the strength to raise my staff.
Master Ming’s mind-mirror reflects and opens a thousand worlds; his gaze pierces through the four continents of Jambudvīpa. Throughout his life he has committed no deeds in the dark;
it is only because of his constant clarity that his hair has turned white.
On the Way through Shanyin, I Stay with the Solitary Old Man of Yunmen.
Last autumn’s ninth month, we parted in Jiangdong. He sits in meditative repose amidst a thousand peaks piled with purple and azure. Last night his roar was heard for a hundred li;
I suspect he has come forth from the mountains for my sake.
A Gift for Attendant Rong of Zhongzhu:
Attendant, you have attained Zen through your practice; there is no need to choose the fire or offer incense again. At the peak of Mount Zhu, the lone monkey’s cry cuts short;
the scent of osmanthus flowers strikes the stone bed sound after sound.
Seeing Master Zhizong Sǒng off as he returns to Nengren to visit his teacher Shizi Huái:
His will soars through ravines and towers above the clouds; you are a second-generation Zhi Dun. There is no need to present the *yuanxiang* (perfect circle)—it has already been wiped away.
A single casket of the heavenly mirror hangs in the clear sky.

Entrusted to the Dharma-treasury, Master Jian-nan’s sword-spirit soars upward to touch the clouds; its divine blade is like autumn water, profound and without a trace. The fierce beasts have been tamed and the dragons have been transformed;
in this era of Great Peace, who recognizes the old general?
Master Rui visited Baoning Heshang, who said:
"The sea crab of the East China Sea, the bamboo shoots of the South Mountain—brought forth, they block the throats of the patch-robed monks.
If the Master wishes to go and clarify this saying, it is much like a cold tide striking a stone.
The eminent first seat Shushan Miaoshou traveled to Min;
the Dwarf Old Man journeyed far into the Min mountains. When the tree fell and the vines withered, he questioned Lan’an. Today, there is no place to sell the meditation mat;
the wooden snake flies out through the Purple Cloud Pass.
Zhong the Venerable Administrator returns to Mount Guiyan. At the same time, he sends this note to Master Chengshan:
"Sleeping on firewood and tasting gall—the resentment fills my breast. In those days of the Dharma-battle, I failed to establish merit; today, longing for home, I seek to uproot once more.
Together with you, I shall topple Mount Zhanqi."
Inquiring after Master Tuimucheng of Yansi: His precept-light shines like the moon upon the assembly of meditators;
he bakes yellow tubers over a pit of dung-fire, fearing only that its pure fragrance might penetrate the Nine Palaces.
Next, in the style of Qingzhuo: Sending off Zen Master Jun to visit his parents— Wind and moon shared equally;
no claim to the merit. The true pulse of Caoxi rejoices in its return to the source. The rush-sandals demand the price of a city of jade;
Hanging them high upon the ten-thousand-fathom eastern sun.
Master Xuán paid homage at the stupa of Wǔzhǔn;
he was a descendant of Yuánzhào. From afar he hastened to follow the tradition and sweep away the dust from the stupa.
In days past, the fire for smelting gold—both gentle and fierce—remains warm even now, as if it were still springtime.
Congratulations on your friend Zhuge’s move to the Shiliao Hermitage.
Having built the Mengtang for a secluded dwelling, he now resides there. This eminent man of the lakes and seas need not be summoned; the broken strings of Dajue have now been mended once more.
Can it be that there is no Buddha-land for Canliao?
The white ox stands exposed in the vast distance, impossible to drive away; its horns and four hooves gleam with silver light. Old Beichen could not cook it;
the spring grasses of the Snowy Mountains naturally waft their fragrance.
The Zen practitioner Xixi has traveled extensively, visiting over a hundred cities; yet upon reaching Mount Ga, it is as if he has never been there before.
King Anala and Jvalamukha—such gateways require one who is capable of ascending them.
Seeing Zen practitioner Ying return to Shu:
the mind-monkey is utterly distressed by the precipices of Jian Gate; the spirit-horse gallops across the Yanyu Rapids.
Having completed his pilgrimage through hundreds of cities of masters, he has returned from his southern quest having won the silken trophy.

Venerable Yuan, the *vina*, bows to the Patriarch and investigates the meaning of that "living" patriarch: there is no need to strike a withered skull. The three-foot cooking cloth is gathered and then spread out;
it is nothing but ten thousand, ten million earthen steamed buns.
Presented to the Head of the Purification Hall:
Intending to continue the "Snow-Hidden Lute" of former years, he urges himself on further in the practice of the Bodhisattva path. Suddenly, amidst his own excrement, he fails to perceive its stench;
with wings sprouted upon his straw sandals, he flies up into the heavens.

Yao Shangren was a man who transcended the four directions, yet the ancients were occupied only with the affairs of donkeys and horses. Coming and going between Xuansha and Xuefeng, he had not yet even managed to warm his meditation cushion;
then again, he traveled from Mount Mao to Tiantong.

When the monk Suishang went traveling, as soon as Liangsu uttered his own name, [Suishang] knew that his lifelong study of sutras and treatises had been in error. He sat firmly upon a large couch, much like Mazu;
there was no need to knock on the door to question the old monk.
Presented to Master Heng:
On that day at Zhaozhou, he met Nanquan. With a courage as vast as heaven, he spoke forthwith, asking: "Among you śrāmaṇeras, who is the master?
This is the profound Chan of the ancient patriarchs, passed down through generations of descendants.
In the Eastern River, the land of China, there are those with the capacity for the Mahāyāna. A hundred thousand have come from the West upon a single reed raft;
having realized directly that the waves are but water, there is no need to gash one's forehead in anticipation of the rising sun at Fusang.
I present this copy of the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* to you, O Monk.

When this sutra first arrived during the Shenlong era, I often lamented that Tiantai could not have encountered it. Only through the Buddha’s proclamation and abundant exhortations was its merit revealed;
I admire how you have transcribed it for wide circulation. Do not follow the frantic delusion of the demon Eṇeya before the mirror, but listen instead to the subtle [voice] of Rāhu.
The bell was struck. The banner of firm vows remained unwearied. In the Jeta Grove, beneath every tree, the autumn wind blew steadily.

This was entrusted to the Elder Master Baoning Mowu, an old recluse dwelling atop Phoenix Terrace. The Tathāgatas of the three ages were swallowed in a single gulp; the imperial decree was proclaimed at the maple-colored steps, and his fame was already established.

Respectfully, the Hall of Censure (the Ministry of Justice) earnestly invited the Honored One Daomi. For the sake of all people, he cast forth the diamond drill; in accordance with this command, he widely opened the gate of nectar.
Among the hundreds and thousands, there are those who possess true knowledge; from the Five Lakes, dragons and elephants vie to hasten toward him.
I send Abbot Yong to visit the ancient master atop the Five-Crested Peak at Jingshan. He sits in the command tent, deploying his strategy like a long serpent;

the old dragon hides its horns and tusks at the bottom of the abyss, while the sleeping tiger reveals its claws and fangs within the pass. This fine monk is like a jade pestle and mortar; this good spiritual friend is like a bowl.
Luo Hua: Who can continue the lute-string of the old master Yantou Xue? A divine colt from Wanwa gallops a thousand miles.

To the Dharma Master Xitian who has come from a hundred-thousand-league journey across the Western Heavens: his two eyes are bright and clear, shining a green light upon people; he relies solely upon the power of the Way and spiritual penetrations.

With power, he deeply investigates the Three Vehicles and the Supreme Vehicle. Like clouds clearing, he flies through the air with his iron staff; in the cool night, he clicks his tongue and recites the Golden Sutra.
If you wish to know the matter of the direct pointing and single transmission, you must listen at the place where the dust of sound ceases.
I send off Attendant Xi; the attendant has attained Zen. A bright pearl is free of flaws, and jade is without blemish. The flash of lightning and the spark from flint display wondrous agility;
the furnace, bellows, tongs, and hammer test the true master. Ten thousand miles of mountains and rivers return to the ultimate reality; the misty waters of a hundred cities are sufficient.
A lifetime’s journey: as you depart, do not resent my silence. From the beginning, I have never scattered sand where there was no vow.

To cultivate wisdom without cultivating merit, or to cultivate merit without cultivating wisdom—when these narrow paths meet, one speaks of long and short. It is simply because the ancient spiritual light has been obscured. At the thousand gates, one should provide offerings to the Arhats.

Han: The White Elephant King, adorned with a hundred jewels, cuts through the waves of the ocean of merit so that its madness subsides; he traverses the path within the forest of wisdom, the fragrance of the flowers of enlightenment spreading.
He sports freely among the various classes of beings, treading majestically upon the ancient field of Buddhas.
Master You wanders on Mount Tiantai;
at the Stone Man’s Crouch by the mouth of the River in Youzhou, his entire being admits not a single dharma to remain. The Gate of Great Dharani is vast across past and present;
the Akṣobhya-eye shines throughout heaven and earth. After the rain passes over the Stone Bridge, one beholds the cliff cascades; when the clouds part atop Huading Peak, one sees [the sun].
At dawn’s first light, the crystal pitcher is utterly devoid of reflection; one should seek out the subtle critiques of Hanshan and Shide.

For a Chan practitioner, the conduct of honoring the patriarchs—whether in action or repose, in use or abandonment—values natural spontaneity. This extraordinary standard and solitary excellence draw near to the Way; contemplate it as a mouth vast enough to swallow the three periods of time.
The Buddha: the colt tramples the people of the world to death. On the towering peaks, the pure regulations remain distinct; at Mount Yangqiao, the successive circular signs are ever new.
One must penetrate the pivot of the Patriarchs’ barrier; do not let it be so easily unfolded as a cooking cloth.
Sending off Abbot Zhong back to Central India:
the mani-jewel within the treasury is utterly unique. Its radiance shoots directly toward the palaces of the Dipper and Ox.

No one has reached the Five Indias; yet before the Thousand-Year Rock, a path leads through. It shines through the aperture of the brain like the moon atop the pine-peak; it perfumes and opens the olfactory faculty like the cassia tree.
Flower Winds. The traces of the numinous are found only where the monkeys cry; do not seek the old tracks by following the crying monkeys.
Master Jian sought that among all worldly affairs nothing is firm, yet only his resolve to dwell in the mountains was lofty. Amidst a heap of dung-fire, he roasted the purple [fungus].

Taro tubers boiled in a bowl of yellow sand alongside mugwort; by the stream, the rustic elder plants bamboo with particular care. Beyond the grove, the immortal master has planted an abundance of peaches.
As long as the master of the hermitage remains, there is no hindrance to finding joy and contentment wherever one may be.
A Sequel to Master Hongzhi’s Verses Left at Guoqing Temple: The jade palace curtains hang as he receives the imperial summons;
The nine-crested auspicious phoenix pecks at the divine *zhī* fungi. Numinous light pierces through the dawning darkness of the masses;

The blade of wisdom rests idly as it unveils the ten thousand phenomena. Sun and moon shine together in the station of Buddhas and Patriarchs; Thunder and lightning resound for a hundred generations of Heaven.
The Teacher of Men: when the total function of the great capacity is at work, what constraints can there be? Within the square it conforms to the square; within the circle it conforms to the compass.
