He tramples through empty space until a path forms of its own accord. Not a single step has ever been taken upon the Buddha-ladder.

The Jade Hare, pregnant, enters through the door; the Golden Cock, brooding its young, cries toward spring. The luster of ink shines brightly upon the cold cliff; the resonance of the Way is clear and cool in the Great Void.
Farewell, West. Turning the position to return to the fundamental capacity, the towering pavilions are lowered by the five clouds.
Sending off Attendant Cheng, the blowing of the cloth-hair awakens the spring of a hundred flowers. Is the Way far? It is true in every encounter; Maitreya’s thousand bodies follow each step.
The wheel turns. For whom does Mañjuśrī extend his single arm? The azure paulownia tree is fit for the phoenix of the Cinnabar Mountain; the golden tether cannot bind the five-colored qilin.
Leaving behind but a single speck of dust upon the tip of the nose, he departs for all quarters to test those who wield the adze.
To Chan practitioner Jian of Luling:

Since the beginning, the Buddha-dharma has never been "yes" or "no. As for the matter of traveling on pilgrimage: the profound intent of Shitou, the *Cantong qi*, the ancestral style of Xiuju, and the *Zhengdao ge*.
Few are those who truly grasp the old man Zhao’s "monk’s robe"; test it by the price of rice in Luling.
The multitude is vast; the light that illuminates heaven and earth remains present. The ancient mirror stands majestic, requiring no polishing.

To send off Master Zhi, speak a single word where wisdom does not reach. Facing him directly, respond skillfully to the immediate occasion. Simply observe the sages of the past and those who followed.

O Sage, from the very beginning there were never six arms or three heads. To clarify that the banner moves while the mind does not move, one must understand that the bridge flows while the water does not.
Having traveled throughout the South to study under various masters, you have now returned to keep me company, O Old Linqiu.
A Gift to Chan Master Chang’an:
A Draft Modeled on Damei Chang Moving his thatched cottage to a remote retreat, he hides away from the world. Wearing lotus leaves as robes, they surpass fine silks and brocades.
Sustaining himself on pine blossoms, he grows weary of rich grain and oil. Monkeys, gibbons, tigers, and leopards share in his meditative joy; Clouds, moon, streams, and mountains are his companions.
The Site of Enlightenment. I wish to retire from the world to pass my twilight years; seeking our old covenant, I come to visit your room amidst the bamboo.
To the attendant Hui, he showed:

"For the patriarchal lineage of wisdom to continue is not difficult. Among the horned there is the qilin; among the winged, the phoenix. This copy of the *Zhijia* (Paper Robe) has been brought forth with fragrant ink."
Weighty! A wisp of cloth blown up in a snowy nest; Tan-yuan did not understand Nanyang’s intent, while Wen-yuan deeply clarified Zhao-lao’s barrier.
Do not say that this mountain elder has no instruction: atop the solitary peak of the Wondrous Mountain, the moon is full and round.
Seeing off Abbot Ning as he returns to Tiantong:
On the clear banks of the River Shao we met by chance; His ancient intent and lofty character are enough to revive the tradition. The golden mallet in his sleeve has long since leaped forth;
The treasure-trove within his breast is naturally brilliant. Like the jade resonating from the sand-basin of Master Zhongfeng, The earth-cakes are sweet as butter—how vast!
I address the Elder: My heart follows the solitary cloud back to my old retreat, where for twenty li the moon shines bright upon the pines and the wind.
Sent to Chief Seat Shibek, morning is leisurely and evening is leisurely; we both think of one another until our hair is white. As for our lot, there is but one monkey and one...
The Crane. Who would discuss the whole ox or the whole elephant? According to his seat in the bowl, there was no Huangbo; pushing forward the master-monks, there was Muzhou.
For you brothers, it does not hinder adding ten characters: the moon shines brightly in the autumn of Danyang Lake.

A Memorial for Attendant Baoning: His Form is Like a Lone Cloud, Unfurling Again after Folding. In the morning he roams the Hundred Yués; in the evening, the Three Wūs. The Vajra Banner faces the Vajra Drill;

upon the Vermilion Phoenix Terrace, a Vermilion Phoenix chick is born. With wisdom, he is like Sima Xiangru returning with his white jade; without artifice, he is like Wangxiang who attained the pearl.
Xuanzhu: "Your teacher Huangbo is no concern of mine; take care not to strike me with your fist like you did at Dayu.

The attendant Meng was sent away while the midsummer heat was like being scorched in a steamer; there was not a moment’s leisure to discuss matters of east and west. Cuiyan has managed to keep his eyebrows."
Presently, at the jade desk, my ears have grown deaf; the Great Way is to be sought through daily diminution. The Sage’s mind must be nurtured to merge with the spring-like ignorance.
Do the masters of various quarters know this? This is the "Great and Small Emptiness" of my own house.

To Master Yundui: The Way resides in the person; its expansion requires diligent effort. Although Huangbo was far away, he was still worthy of emulation. The cypress tree before the courtyard shall attain Buddhahood;
this very branch of peach blossoms exists within the cave. When the day comes that Kebin’s heart is truly resolved, it will be the command of Xinghua.
While traveling, Mount Mao was entirely submerged; my local sentiments remain with me. I intend to cast a golden statue of Ziqi. Sent by Lun Zhongfang of Baoning:
"The mountain wind blows up the clouds from Fuyan; arising spontaneously, it stands far beyond the common crowd. It soars through the dragon’s lair across the three tiers."
Waves surge; at the Phoenix Terrace, nine-tufted plumage dances. On Plum Island, spring warmth brings flowers like snow. In the chamber of leeks, years have passed yet the flesh remains warm.
Elder and younger brothers play the *xun* and *chi* flutes in turn; who in the human world does not hear them?
Sending the attendant Jujing to Jinling—tree fallen, vine withered;
laughter never ceases. The single cotton robe has been sold away, leaving no further cause for concern.
Upon a single hair-tip is a golden lion; within five hundred [minds] is a living steed. At the edge of the bright crane is Bao Gong’s stupa; where the blue dragon soars is the Emperor’s [palace].
Wangzhou: Amidst the shadows of the autumn wind, he flies with his monk’s staff; in silence, he listens to the cold tide striking the stones.
Presented to Zelan of Jiyuan:
A rare Udumbara flower illuminating the world with its wondrous fragrance; a single stream from Xunxi flows forth from Cao’an. Wind and moon are shared equally at Yunfeng.
Atop the peak, golden Jeta Grove is spread out; wearing the talisman behind the elbow, he deceives the Buddhas and Patriarchs. With eyes like those of Maheśvara, he illuminates heaven and earth.
Do not begrudge the narrow ground for being unable to contain his dance; the Way of Fengxue and Yangqi is self-sufficient.
Xie Yu fashioned the sculpted image of the founding patriarch for the West Hall;

it was modeled after the lineage of Master Cuiwei of Jingzhao. For five hundred years, this ancient sage has remained steadfast: his eyes possess the double pupils of a sovereign, radiating brilliant light;

his hands hang below his knees as he sits with majestic dignity. How does the stone stand, supported from within the void? Only when jade is hidden within the mountains does its brilliance begin to shine.
Radiance bursts forth, revealing a seamless, round stupa; the cloud peaks grow more majestic as the tiger’s prowess increases.
Sent to Master Jixiu of Jinshan:
I recognize Pingzhou as my ancestral home. Elder brother, you ceaselessly beat the "poisonous drum. Two pairs of clay oxen fight their way in.

The ocean is vast; secluded birds warble as they scold the falling blossoms. With accumulated greenery, the Way is lofty and the pearl is free of flaw; with silent resonance, his fame is weighty and the jade is without blemish.
Do not forget the entrustment of the former master: chew the void thoroughly, yet do not spit out the core.
Presented to the Abbot Chengtian Jian:
The Buddha-dharma of Caoxi is utterly free from triviality. When facing honey, what need is there to further speak of its sweetness? Take up and examine this diamond circle;
how does it compare to the sharp tip of a drill on a carriage? It breaks through the white waves for thousands of miles and leaps upon the blue heavens—three...
Zuzhan’s *Chants on the Foot of a Toad*: "Better to face the single mirror before Vipaśyin; Right now, roll up the 'Night-Bright' curtain.
In the same rhyme, a gift to Secretary Xiong as he travels between the two capitals:

"He has brought the fragmentary tongue of Ciming to a standstill; The old woman’s discernment has its own underlying reason. Before the thatched hut was even pitched, he stood alone on the solitary peak."
Abiding. A golden staff first roamed between the two palaces; before a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, one rode a spirited steed. Upon waters of a thousand tiers, one hung a lantern ball.
The Master’s wisdom and eloquence were difficult to match; he answered with nothing but a single silence from Vimalakīrti.
Attendant Yi returned to Tianyi, while also selecting Duanjiang Wenheshang. Borrowing the rhyme of Master Zhuyuan, who was ninety years of age:
"The old man Duanjiang sits in meditation at the ancient Brahma-palace on Lotus Peak; do not say his furnace and bellows for smelting gold have grown cold."

Cold. It would empty the horse herds of Jibei. At times one hears the sound of bells and pestles amidst the moonlight of a thousand peaks; in stillness one listens to the sighing of pines in the winds of ten thousand ravines.
Please inquire for me with great courtesy whether you are well: north of the Yue River and east of Lake Jian.
Presented to Jiàn at Xītáng. Visiting Old Monk Tóuyǔ of Chūnyǔ Ān:
In the Chūnyǔ Hermitage dwells a blue-eyed barbarian; The furnace for smelting gold remains as it was of old. Turtle-hair and rabbit-horns fill the counting-chambers;
Snake-legs and salt-fragrance abound on the roads. How could fine wine be restricted to deep alleys? Vinegar’s sourness does not depend on its volume.
Hulu. When the banquet in Wuzhong was concluded, he returned to pay his respects. He also applied himself to the protection against the coarse blows and shouts [of Chan].
He escorted the head of the repentance service back to Xiazhu, where he rejoiced at the reopening of the Dharma seat of Master Yugang Ciyun.
In this age, he is an elder of vast talent and eloquence; the precious stupa has emerged from the golden ground.
He departed; from Lingfeng he flew toward the land of India. Master Wuzhuo cremated his body, leaving only his image behind; Master Xuanzang translated the scriptures, yet the platform remains.
Departing from here, you shall ascend the high seat when the academic examinations are held, sharing the wind and moon to revitalize the Hengtai tradition.

As the Abbot Lukzang travels to Fuzhou, the tidal waters of the "spirit-tower sea" flow like a level road. He need not fear the coarse waves upon the barbarian junks. Within the city stand the two towers, East and West;
there is a single pavilion for drums and horns that has no peer beneath heaven. Though the local dialects of that land require interpretation, the spiritual worth of this monk remains beyond measure.
One must be soaked in it. Lychees, olives, grapes, and oranges—the thornbush and golden ring are not like them.
Sending Upadeśaka Yi to visit Master Zhuyuan’s disciple and pay homage at the Stone Bridge on Mount Tiantai:
if he does not meet a true teacher, he will not rest until his purpose is fulfilled. You should know that this is like Liangsu’s visit to Mazu.
The valley is like Yunmen’s meeting with Muzhou. On Mount Zituo, you must exert yourself; in the swift waters of Xianyuan, you may ride the current.
You must firmly grasp the bamboo staff that accompanies you; the path is slippery—beware of the stones.
Chen Xiyan came to visit me. I compose this in response, following his rhyme:
The books and transmissions within your breast flow richly and freely; Yet you refuse to ascend the Moon Palace, though it lies but a foot away.

A reclusive gentleman reclining high atop the tower, Comes to view the monk who keeps his door shut by the stream. How many pairs of sandals will the spring mountains consume? In the night rain, one cannot forget the ten... [lines omitted].
Carrying lamps, we both remain restless in our later years; do not say that you have never seen anything beneath the forest trees.
Once this mind is realized, O Master Liaoxin, one will sit securely at Mount Tiantai and Mount Yan;
until this mind is realized, one wanders from west to east, carrying a staff over six or seven feet long.

A footstep, yet the mountains ahead remain unknown, numbering in the thousands. Ming, Yue, Tai, and Wen are the lairs of dragons and elephants; there, celestial incense and auspicious snow gather in sandalwood thickets.
Seek instruction from the old Chan master of Yongjia: a single orb of river moon shines upon the pines and the wind.
Presented to the Abbot Chengtian Yuanzang.

Wandering through the lands of the rising and setting sun in eastern Zhejiang, By the waters of the east and west streams of the King— Deep, firm, secluded, and remote, where no one reaches; One must surely believe in the Way of the Sage.
The ordinary mind is the Way; it is the mani-jewel within the Tathāgatagarbha. Its radiance shines brilliantly, illuminating the dark alleys.
All that you have used throughout your life is precisely this; there is no need to push out a compass to find your way.
Wahongulin Dongzhou. For the sake of the hermitage’s verse, the Master of the Ink-Trace School proclaims:
"Establishing a formidable barrier, he sweeps away the great mountain at the gate; within the glowing coals and boiling cauldrons, one achieves perfect awakening;
the mountains of knives and trees of swords are as if they were mere trifles. Xiujū raises the diamond drill, and primordial awareness unfolds its iron [tongs].
The countenances [of the Buddhas]—though the two gates of the nectar have long been closed—the tide rises at Hepu and the pearl returns.
To the Abbot Jizang of Lingyin:
eyes raised like those of Mahesvara, a talisman fastened at the elbow; with a scale that has no stars, he determines the smallest fraction. He cleaves open the mountains of the land of Chu.
Jade: Gathering the pearl within the Tathāgatagarbha, briefly revealing the Compassionate Brightness’s horizontal water-sword.
Not carrying Magu into the garden to hoe, the "thousand-li shared breeze" verse of the Way-man is black ink written upon white paper without cause.

On a Boat on the Wusong River: This journey, undertaken for the sake of inspiration, sees me drifting upon the Wusong. Who is this elder, free from artifice, upon the sea? As the setting sun rises with the tide, waves surge through a thousand estuaries;
A returning sail catches a single river wind sent by heaven. Beyond the vast expanse lies a crescent moon of cool light; In the distance, a few specks of green mountains fade away.
Amidst the mist, I gaze afar at the path by the mountain stream; the autumn wind has fully opened the jade lotuses.
Sent to Elder Chūn of Sōrin—his reputation for the Way resounds like that of Genpō; without leaving his perch, he sees the master, sitting firm at Sōrin, opening the tiger’s den.

The Cave: My elder brother drew the whale’s tusk from the depths of the Dharma-sea; the wooden ball still retains enough warmth to roll, and the clear resonance of the stone drum is sufficient for striking.
I, an old man adrift on rivers and lakes, have nothing to give as a gift; three thousand miles away, I pluck the willow blossoms.

Presented to the Abbot Nuozang: A crane standing tall upon Vulture Peak; with the markings of an elephant or dragon, his presence is so majestic it startles all who behold him. The vastness of Yunmeng Lake is swallowed within his breast;

the breadth of misty waves makes the Wu Mountains seem small before his eyes. He provides offerings at the expense of fines, spreading out a jade-like banquet; he answers those who seek instruction from monks with pearls.
Running on a platter; the decrepit old man fails to follow the Boatman’s command. His song from the oars serves as a mere substitute for emerald jade.

Lamenting the life-long entanglements of the exceptionally brilliant Chan Master Mingji, they remain even more gnarled and twisted. He leaves this venerable lord of Lingxiao at a standstill. He splits apart Mount Hua and beats the iron drum.
The drum beats; plowing open the Eastern Sea, one plants the jade flower. The lion that turns its body leaves no trace;
the horned hare does not bared its fangs. As the predecessors have faded away, there is only sighing and regret. Now who is the guiding chariot?
The Chan Master Xie Mao, known as Puxie Yunlin, brought forth from his sleeve the "Muzhou Straw Sandals. Having offered them to his mother, he has now extended them to me.

Like the several pairs of clogs worn by Hui Lingyun during his excursions, or the pair of webbed sandals used by Zi Qiao for his travels, these pearl-encrusted slippers once found their way to the royal court, yet these hempen shoes have reached the imperial dais.
Above there is nothing; what does it matter if others are soft? Let the old monk remain here to keep company with those in full-lotus posture.
At Chengtian, attendant Zhen bows before the Patriarchs;
the ancestral courtyard is like a crouching tiger and a coiling dragon. Pluck the weeds and gaze at the wind—look closely! For a thousand years, Shaoshi has been without a shadow.
The tree; the seven hundred Huangmei mud-clods. When the duck flies, it drags off Xiong峰’s nose; when the cock crows, it throws open Yuanwu’s barrier.
All eighty-four men have been pressed down and passed through; one gulp of the West River must leave it utterly dry.
The Elder Benevolent King’s staff is long;

the third arrival is the great function of the patch-robed monk, precisely the occasion for skillful means. The chestnut thorn and the golden circle are at his disposal to spit out or swallow. The Buddha of the Sun’s Face is the same as the Buddha of the Moon’s Face;
the Honored One Benevolent King is none other than the Honored Dharma King. In years past, we drank from the same small stream together; three times he has come to strike the True.
The Gate of Purity. Fortunately, the ancestral estate remains. Beneath the golden incense burner lies the iron K'un-lun.

Together with the verse for Tianquan’s Far Bank, this is presented as a gift to Huazang, the Venerable Life-keeper (Weina), as he travels through Zhejiang East, Jiangnan North and South, and Zhejiang West and East.
With a single staff, he wanders away, his spirit full of zest. He pours out thirty thousand [verses] from Tianquan.
A single sail on another shore borrowed from him; Mount Potalaka surges with the sea as the moon rises at the third watch.
At Fangguang Temple, the midnight bell is heard; reaching the place where Nuo sits crouched, a flying dragon hangs above the thousand-fathom pool.

Presented to Seongbong Injeon upon his return to Min, sharing a drink by the waters of the Yeoncheon River: Accidentally meeting three thousand *li* away, This flying arrowhead from Snowy Peak— How does it compare to Yangqi’s chestnut thorn?
When leaving the ridge, it was the time of the plum and bean; Upon arriving home, it is precisely the season for lychees.
Branches red. Someone asked about the pine and the moon: "An old man with white snow covering his head.
Elder An was sent forth to take charge of the world;
his fragrant name, Huiri, leaped out as all raised shouts of joy. Wǎngxiàng, having no mind, naturally obtained the pearl. At the thousand-fathom numinous pool, he creates the sweet nectar.
Zhai: A single wheel of the sun of wisdom shines upon the dark thoroughfare; the "Old Man of the Western Crags" is still warm in his flesh. The Chan elder Chunyu’s virtue is not solitary;
I imagine him afar, striking the lethal "Poisonous Drum," its sound heard throughout the hundred Yue and three Wu regions.
The Venerable Huaren follows the teaching as the thatch fills the hall; a thousand li of silver moon share one sky. One must not hope to polish a brick into a mirror;
first, learn to sow the field to earn one's rice. Mazu’s single shout still resounds; Baizhang’s second visit to study the dialogue remains.
The circle is finally complete. When Luzu saw a monk, he simply faced the wall; only Old Nanquan understood this.
In his exchange of verses, he lost the "barbarian" [the monk].
Master Baichuanhai’s profound Buddhist dharma is as deep as the sea; the hundred rivers compete to flow day and night, yet fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs know not its depths.
Life! Mosquitoes and gadflies, asuras—once satiated, they rest; there is no need to seek the wish-fulfilling jewel in abundance.
It takes but a single tug upon the head of the six tortoises to sport amidst a thousand waves and ten thousand billows, gathering up a single hook of coral moonlight.
The Librarian Benjue (Zhao Benjue) brought forth Lia'an Zhongmou’s expositions and sought a colophon from Xie Li Dan.
Single-handedly wielding the "Ghost-Seeing-Sorrow" [sword], he picked up the Hundred-Flower Ball cast by Chiyang. Who can compare to this Father, who dwells in seclusion?
Old man! When a son is born, he should be like the venerable Zhongmou. Appearing and disappearing amidst the sparks of flint and flashes of lightning; fists come and kicks go, ever more graceful.
The myriad rivers flow back and forth, transmitting the news; upon the ten-thousand-li long river is but a single leaf-boat.
In Lamentation for Chan Master Guangzhi Quanwu of Longxiang Xiaoyin, Who Held His Four Abodes at Famous Mountains to Fulfill His Original Vow:
Deep within the Dragon River, he moored his floating cup; He widely opened the ocean of wisdom and poured forth ambrosia.
He fully awakened to the gate of the profound, thundering the Dharma-thunder; As the dust of debate was just rising, it suddenly fell to the ground; The banner of victory stood high, yet suddenly—
Startled and shattered. With a casual laugh, he turns his body and departs; the tide shakes the empty city, but it cannot call him back.
Presented to Chengtian Maonazana. In Jiangxi, pay homage to the Patriarchs;
rejoice that the Great Matter is already concluded. Why must you seek elsewhere beyond? Turning his body on Yaoyao Peak, a true lion.
Disciple, in the open air is the water-buffalo of Mount Shui; within the tattered cotton robe is hidden the ultimate treasure; inside the bronze sandal is filled with oil.
Before the wind, everyone is invited to offer three prostrations; eighty-four people all nod their heads in agreement.
Presented to Chan Master Tong of Wanshou:

Returning to Weiyang, I have attained that one transmission of Gautama; The four quarters and eight directions are naturally lucid and resonant. The ocean of three thousand worlds is a treasury of radiant light;
The willow breezes of the twenty-four bridges. I cast back my scroll of verse to the Elder Chan-yueh; May the sound of the horn awaken Great...
Master Yuan Gong: The *qionghua* flower is truly of no ordinary stock; it gathers the celestial fragrance within its sleeves.

To Yuwang’s Chan Master Qiong, who has thoroughly penetrated the supreme, highest mechanism of our school: holding a bald broom upside down to paint the brows of a beauty—throughout his life he has harbored this jade; who could [fathom] it?
Consciousness: the power of meditative concentration is like a mountain, immovable. A sleeping tiger among the assembly of Yuanwu; a phoenix chick at the gate of Nanyang.
In years to come, upon the curved wooden meditation seat, he will bitterly revile the old, ancient sage of Caoxi.

Presented to the Abbot Qi of Yuwang Monastery: The Sūtras Return to the Canon, and Chan Returns to the Sea. The sea possesses the sūtras, while the canon possesses Chan. One plucks the Southern Dipper and settles it in the Northern Dipper;
one shifts the Eastern Land to the Western Quarter. The true-body relics shall endure for a thousand years; the legacy of the Great Awakened One remains for countless ages.
A hundred years. Today, because you crossed the stream, my heart has once again arrived before Mount Mao. Presented to Chan Master Jing of Lingyin.
In this auspicious age, Mingzu, the magistrate of Taicheng in Fenghua, can discern even the finest hairs;
phoenixes in the marshes and qilin in the wilds cannot escape his gaze. There has never been one who travels far...
To abide, one must first descend before one can ascend. The Patriarchs possessed their own true adze; the royal armory never held such a blade.
Across the seventy-two marshes, the mist and waters are emerald green; they hold aloft the horns of a hare and the hair of a tortoise.
A Gift for the Abbot □ of Donglin: Returning to the East Sea, the face of Mount Lu remains as it ever was;
yet after this encounter, its spirit appears ancient and weathered. Eighteen noble sages have polished their chariots, and over five thousand scrolls of the *Prajñāpāramitā* reside within his bowl.
For many years, the dream of the butterfly has been a constant visitor to his household; across ten thousand li of whale-waves, he rests upon a reed raft.
It may be traversed. In Sanskrit this means "attaining the capital city" (dūìdé). There is not a single further dharma to be deliberated upon.
Together with the Venerable Yuansou, I present this to the Abbot An:
For twenty years you have sat preaching the Dharma atop Mount Lingxiao; you cast the "thorny plum" and the "golden circle" at will; the wooden horse and the clay ox are utterly extinguished.
Rest. Śākyamuni and Maitreya may discuss their meeting; for the sake of others, he descended several times into the Dragon’s Cave. With a trusting foot, he kicked over the Golden Phoenix’s Nest.
A horned iron snake cannot penetrate it—look at that single blade of *máohú* grass after the fire has passed.

At Píngjiāng, the Master Lì of Huànzhù requested [this eulogy] for the Elder Huànzhù, who has an illusory grandson: Standing tall and upright, he revives this culture; The three dots of the circle are the eye of Maheśvara.
Steep and lofty, he is a single gate of nectar. In the dense sandalwood forest dwells the lion; Upon the tiered stone pagoda shines the white [moon].
Massed like clouds: the remaining majesty and lingering wind of our late father remain. He did not begrudge his compassion in receiving those who followed him.
Dengshang bows before the Patriarch; his rush-sandals hang toward the city of Muzhou. For a thousand years, he continues the night lamp before the cliff. Mazu’s colt has the talent to leap.
Leap! Yangqi’s donkey trots about, prancing its hooves. At Donglin there is still an old man planting lotuses; at Nanyue there is now no monk roasting yams.
Having traveled through tiger dens and demon palaces, he returns, snapping a branch of rattan cane in two.
The Record-keeper Ran of Mount Jingshan returns to Wenzhou;
his vast and heroic spirit fills the realm. Among the disciples of Xuedou, he is a peerless master. Su Dongpo’s ink-well serves as a field for his divine calligraphy;
Liu Lang’s peach tree grows with flourishing branches. The rows of rocks at Geese Peak add to its wondrous beauty, like the brilliant pearls from the jaws of a black dragon.
Diverse and scattered. Where accumulated greens and silent sounds allow the lute-string to continue, even the trees and grasses of the forest flourish with vitality.
As for the farewell to Venerable Yuni of Mount Gui:
In his youth, Chijue was at Mount Gui; He received the single stream from Cao’an. The ocean is vast; let the giant tortoise turn as it will.

To the side, the heavens are so high they can accommodate the soaring flight of cranes. I feel ashamed before the Patriarch Xiong-feng regarding our Way; I envy you, whose name is equal to that of the Elder Duanji.
You have emerged with such agility and soar across the sky—strive with diligence! From of old, the customs of Min and Shu have been one and the same.
South of Mei Ling, I have fashioned an endless lamp;
within the lamp there is a mirror, and as the lamp is endless, the mirror has no external lamp—it even feels ashamed. The ten dharma-realms divide into a thousand dharma-realms;
one divine continent illuminates the four divine continents. Mount Sumeru constantly serves as the wick of its radiance, and the seawater is frequently replenished by wisdom.
The oil of wisdom, even if blown upon by the Vairambha winds, cannot be extinguished. The mind of the Zen elder is like the lunar orb in autumn;
the intent of the site of enlightenment is infinite.

Adorning the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with the great beings of the various heavens, twenty celestial bodies manifest as emanations, acting as both leaders and companions descending into the mundane world. Seated upright amidst jeweled necklaces upon the vajra-throne.
Stone armor newly ranks him among the jade shoots; his compassionate countenance as he preaches the Dharma appears like the moon. His precious mace that crushes demons strikes terror into men;
on the mats of the Jasper Pond, his merit is infinite. Five-colored rays of light illuminate the azure waves.
I send Master Kong to pay homage at the stupa of Venerable Dugu:
At the head of the old hermitage on Vulture Peak, A dream follows the waters of the Qiantang River. Fortune and wisdom are both complete; a thousand matters are fulfilled.
The two words "death" and "life" cease at once. The dragon roars in the withered tree as the jade spring grows cold; The ape howls in the empty mountains as the jade wind rises high.
Autumn trees; with a spade slung across the shoulder, one strikes the spirit pagoda. Where can one find the Wu-dynasty sword by marking the boat?
On which mountain was the bell cast that the sound of the whale is heard from the small stream? It is at this time that rites and music are restored. When Rāhu strikes, the multitudes are startled.
Deaf. When Yuanliang heard it, he knitted his two brows. Deep and resonant, the thunderous drum ceases its bitter course; vast and clear, the frosty tones stir the pure precepts.
The green stone of Central India remains unharmed today; I can only think longingly of the Teacher, the Tamer of Men, who dwells in Kośala.
Entrusting virtue to the solitary clouds, encouraging the Mount Ao, and settling the snowy mind—these three masters reside in the secluded stone chambers of the lush green peaks of Jingfeng.
Divided like the three legs of a tripod, they exchange verses in mutual praise. The six men of Fenshui have become great vessels;
the three Buddhas of Dongshan are of one stream. The Sūtras return to the Canon and Zen returns to the Sea; as the bow is learned from Ji, so too is the smith’s art.
Having mastered the art of the "sheepskin" (the Zen robe), he has thoroughly deliberated upon the matters of the "axe-head" (the Zen staff). Simultaneously, he kicks out the hundred-flower ball.
He sends off Master Ling-shi back to Tiantai;

his fame fills the heavens like the *huangzhong* pitch-pipe. Ten thousand monks take refuge in him, crowding like elephants and dragons, as he vigorously shakes the profound net and transcends the deaf.
The Patriarch practiced the ancient Way at Mount Zhongfeng; the teachings of Yongming were like a vast lake.
A world-renowned master and centenarian—whose "White Snow" melody is so lofty, who would dare to harmonize it? For now, let us join Han and Shi as they caress the solitary pine.

I thank Master Duangjiang for coming so far to see me off; three prostrations to Great Plum (Daming). Amidst the cries of the flying squirrel, one dream unfolds. Once the immortal has departed, it is hard to follow him—Master Mei;
once the tiger is gone, who will protect Xiangyang? The rattling bamboo sedan passes along the winding sheep-gut path; the peaked cloth cap is as lofty as a crane’s.
Hair turning white with age; there is no need to lament the narrowness of the dance floor for the sleeves. The pine blossoms possess a lingering fragrance for a thousand years.

Presented to the Librarian Zhangzhu Lingming, whose fame and reputation are known for their pure character: the Buddha-dharma has not yet declined today. Within the Chamber of Ambrosia, the hundred flowers bloom.

Sweet wine. Beneath Mount Jiyun, there were four willow branches. Having come from afar to Wuyue to seek out a kindred spirit, before even stepping onto the boat’s gunwale, I present these as a gift for the painful oars.
Do not take offense at their lack of substance; they offer nothing to chew upon. The spring wind and spring rain are blowing most desolately.

Sending off the monk to pay homage to the Patriarchs throughout Jiangxi and Hunan: a thousand hills and ten thousand mounds of *luantan* stupas. Many are the "Grandfathers" with mouths like winnowing baskets;
few are the "Rocks" who skillfully handle the fishing line. Entering Tengwang Pavilion from the Western Hills, the Yellow Crane soars over and overturns the Parrot Isle.
Wuyou Island: losing the eyes, yet picking up the nose. Riding the ox, there is no need to seek the ox further.
A rabbit-horn staff is long indeed; a rabbit horn is fit to serve as a staff. Lady Heng-er plants it with her own hands in the moon; what grows from Zhongshan is full of guile.
The root of this rogue cannot be nourished by the lowlands. The moon of cassia is pushed forth across ten thousand li; Mount Taihua stands revealed through its thousand peaks.
At the point where the withered banana is pulled up, the presence or absence of gain and loss shall be verified when it arrives.

A whisk made of tortoise hair, scraped from the back of a tortoise—this is fit for a Buddha. When discussing the profound mystery, one does not compare the short with the long. When hung up, both demons and Buddhas hide their six senses;

when raised aloft, humans and devas listen to its proclamation. Striking through the mysterious barrier, it clarifies regret and fortune; knocking it into shape, it forms an auspicious omen that cuts off all [delusion].
He accepted it. Zhaozhou’s utilization was inexhaustible; even at the end, he still entrusted it to the Prince of Zhao.
To Master Rong, Curator of Zhongzhu:
A slumbering tiger before Thousand-Year Rock, a phoenix chick atop the Terrace of Jinling. When it leaps forth, it unfolds its nine-fold plumage.

An auspicious omen: when the light of the eyes opens, its radiance shakes for a hundred paces. Its majesty does not fall into the various directions, for the golden net is dense. One must guard against the peril of the brocade loom upon level ground.
Soaring and flying far upward to a height of a thousand fathoms, the entire assembly within the pipe is not easily perceived.

Sending Attendant Yù to visit the Master at the place where Little Jade calls out repeatedly: the rooster by the railing serves as the catalyst; it is intended solely for Kāśyapa to understand, and not permitted for the Old Barbarian to know.
Lips like waves of water, snow-white; the moon on Mount Tai resembles a brow. A potent phrase from the road—returning, I ask the Master of the Deer City.
The Master Yuan (abbot of Ding-shui) replies:
"He recognized the Patriarch’s golden arrow method; having cast off the pack-saddle, he has shed the head-cage. Cutting across the stream, he is truly a fragrant elephant."
O King, how can a raging inferno allow even a mosquito to alight? The Dharma Master of Yongdong is capable of the most extraordinary feats;

he would use a blade of grass as a rope to bind empty space. Knowing such matters, one should simply let them rest; why does this donkey-like fellow wait for another moment to catch a glimpse? You sent a gāthā to me, promising to come in autumn;
you were prepared to break the meditation seat during our intense discourse. Do you know or not that the path at Shitou is slippery? Take firm hold of your feet!
Guard against falling into a trap. Send forth the Zen practitioner Ming: clearly see the head of the hundred grasses;

clearly see the intent of the Patriarchs. A clever person seizes it and goes; as for those who are deluded and confused— *Note: This is a prose commentary on a verse. The final phrase "矇憧底" (mōng chōng de) is an incomplete or colloquial fragment indicating those who lack clarity.*
Simply nodding off to sleep. White jade is flawless; bright pearls are free of blemish. Straw sandals are dried in the sun, awaiting the autumn wind;
where not a blade of grass grows for thousands of miles.
A verse for sending Master Zong back to his village:
"Having words or being without words—wisteria leaning against a tree. Setting down the earthenware basin, one cannot stop laughing. A true lion bites;

who would be willing to lean on another's gate or dwell by another's door? The capacity of this seeker of the Way is like an ancient bronze vessel and its stand; From the tip of his staff, he strikes forth the void."
The marrow of emptiness is not like a short man selling a cloth banner, vainly traveling three thousand five hundred li. Cease your studies, gather your things, and return home;
even Daowei’s mouth of laughter dare not open. If the venerable masters of Min possess the eye, I shall build for you a lofty golden terrace.
Two recluses in cold crags: one Cool and Clear, the other Golden and Majestic. Two lacquer buckets, poverty to the very bone. One man’s eyes weigh eight *liang*;
another’s nostrils are exactly half a *jin*. Five peaks and twin streams, the path through the pine gate; two lacquer buckets, incense-filled.
Heavenly Wealth! One man drapes a lion robe low; another ties his elephant-king trousers high. A half-moon hangs from the tip of an old willow branch;
one claps his hands while the other points it out. Failing to realize this meaning yourself, you instead say that the practice of cultivation is merely bitter toil.
The bamboo tube has been lost and there is no place to find it; picking up a broom, let us at least offer some consolation. Talkative fellow!
Fenggan departs and does not return; ten thousand ages of pure wind, a single piece of fine silk.

Sent to Master Yushu: The *maṇi* jewel within the treasury of the teacher at Mount Guiyan— People of past and present do not recognize it. Master Yongjia Zhenjue once pointed it out directly before our eyes.
In the bright moon one sees white; in the dark moon one sees black. The wise do not seek it through the absence of mind, yet it is naturally attained.

At the beginning of the month of waning, the excellence of Mount Yan was hidden and stored away with profound intimacy; once it suddenly manifested, the great thousandfold world-system was illuminated through and through.
Carrying it back, he presented it to the Master. He spoke clearly of this wondrous matter: "Do you not see the great Peng riding through the eye of a lotus fiber?
In an ordinary moment, he knocks down the moon from the edge of the sky."
Presented to Attendant白玉 (Baiyu) within the Cloud-Companion Chamber:

White clouds are originally unconfined things; they take the cold and simple as their body and idleness as their bone. Whether spreading or curling, whether departing or remaining—who accompanies them?
Only the bright moon. The mind of the Way-person is one with the bright moon; thus, the white clouds come again and again.
We follow one another; facing each other in the mountain crags, we both remain silent. Be careful not to be carried away by the east wind or the west wind;

I only fear that the man of the Way will leave the mountains. Upon the rock there is no one to accompany him as he dwells with the clouds. If the man of the Way departs, even the clouds will be in haste; when the moon is bright, neither can find the other.
Presenting the attendant Benzhen with the Golden Immortal’s Iron Mask: Summoned, he does not come; pushed, he does not go away. The tuft of cloth was plucked off but never blown upon.
The golden sun flies up onto the coral tree. The affairs of the Zen school are no trivial matter; turning the body, one ascends directly to the hundred-foot pole.
A bamboo pole a foot long; throughout the worlds of the ten directions the wind whistles, and from the blazing heavens snowflakes fly vast and wide.
Zhongfeng breaks the sand bowl; Songyuan fashions a broom. At midday he strikes the third watch; facing south, he gazes at the Big Dipper.
In every shrine and every speck of dust is the gate of nectar; in every thing and every instance is the lion’s roar.
Seeing Master Fafa returning to Chaling:
The humble donkey of Chaling has its horns broken; A thousand ages of pure wind stir the vast void. A single bright pearl, its value equal to a city;
The empty sky shakes with golden bells. Master Fafa’s home is likewise in Chaling; The son of West Mountain wields his iron [staff].
Niusun saw the Boatman upon the river at Huating; with a single stroke of his oar, the waves surged. Now he sings once more the tune of returning home;
for my sake, send word to Yù of Cháling: "The mountains and rivers before our eyes are as ancient as they are now; the white clouds have snapped their strings—who shall continue them?"
I present three rafters to the abbot of the hermitage;
a thousand great halls are but a single seven-foot span. Throughout his life, everyone has received what he used;

beneath these three rafters, one makes their livelihood. Who is the guest beneath these three rafters? For six years on the Snowy Mountains, there was not even a single rafter; the magpie’s nest rested upon his crown amidst the reeds.
Knees pierced through; at Shaolin for nine years he did not hold the broom. Sitting coldly and motionless, he faced the wall in vain. Zhaozhou pulled down the curtain and departed;
in the end, he did not recognize the master of the hermitage. Two clay oxen fight and do not turn back; the hundred birds carrying flowers have nowhere to go.
They overturn the three rafters until it is utterly bare; below there is no place to plant a staff, above there is no tile. A hundred billion...
Heaven and earth are encompassed within it; from this, the value of these three rafters is enhanced.

Sent to the Abbot Guo of Jiangshan for his prostrations before the Dharma-body of the Great Being at Mount Potalaka—which is as vast as space: the Great Being’s compassionate heart is like the great ocean, which the world seeks to measure with a ruler.

Emptiness. Furthermore, one might wish to hold a conch-shell to measure the waters of the ocean; if empty space could be measured and the ocean could be fathomed, that person would indeed be equal to a Great Being.
Upon a single hair-tip are infinite bodies, and within each body’s hair-pores are oceans as numerous as the atoms of all lands.

From these, one extracts the ancient ruler and square of Master Zhigong; everywhere is the Gate of Perfect Penetration. Having recovered the pearl from within the *maṇi* treasury, it does not belong to the center.
The current flows to the other shore; upon the Pan-t'o rock, the sun’s disc is crimson. The Dharma-body of the Great Being is fully revealed.
While traveling to Zhanggong Cave, I compose a poem in the rhyme of the Celestial Master to present to Chen Jingshan:
In the ancient celestial grotto of Khan-ha, the breeze is cool; The brocade screens and jade pillars shimmer with golden light. The Spirit Official of a thousand years laughs as he welcomes me.
Guest: With silvered beard, rosy cheeks, and long, azure brows, he climbs the perilous heights, forgetting the first steps. The immortal elder gives me the dew of the jade flower;
from where does this cry of a phoenix come? A jade youth points afar toward the path of mist and clouds.
The Arhat crosses the sea;
at the Gate of the Sea, ten-thousand-fathom surging waves crash. Within the whirlpools of the watery palace, forms appear and vanish. Colorful banners and feathered canopies sway in the misty void.
Golden nails and vermilion doors gleam with translucent brilliance. The Dragon King and Hai’er are both solemn and harmonious, escorting him forth as he emerges from the eighteenth [gate].
O Hero of the World! Whether trailing behind or leading the vanguard, one treads upon the jade whisk to boast of supernormal powers;
another upholds a precious pagoda with two azure pupils. One brandishes a feather fan to spread the pure breeze; another holds a *kamandalu* revealing a multi-storied pavilion.
One plants a staff like the red mandarin fish; another tilts a wind-hat like a spreading thistle. One old man sits cross-legged, a ghostly artisan; another draws forth [the sword].
Pai-ta rides a green steed; one treads upon a lion’s head with disheveled hair; one sits upon a cooking cloth with garments draped over his head;
one wears a Zen robe and stands amidst leaping eels; one plays with a precious jewel while gazing at a blue dragon; one displays a protruding belly and plucks two children.
One monk with a golden staff has the strength of an elephant; one general, about to reach the shore, is like a rainbow.
One sits upon a sheep-cart, hurrying along; another straddles a large, brindled tiger. One burns incense of *guggulu*, thick and lush;

the mountain spirit comes forth to welcome him with devotion and respect. Armored warriors arrive in endless throngs; at the Fangguang Monastery, the evening bell tolls as it hangs high from the treetops.
The golden stirrups are crimson; monkeys, gibbons, tigers, and leopards clamor amidst the mountain thickets. The procession enters straight for the peaks of Tiantai.
Looking back, one beholds the Anavatapta Lapis Lazuli Palace. Cherish well, O venerable elder of Sāgara!
Seeing Yangshan’s Chief Seat Yin return to Jiangshan:
"The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the blind donkey is extinguished; the Patriarch’s Heart-Seal, the iron-ox mechanism.
Master Baogong’s twelve-faced Avalokiteśvara, the four rattan branches beneath Jiyun Peak—how does this compare to Muzhou carrying a single board? Is it thus, or is it not?"

He also eradicated [all traces], toppling Yunmen’s "One-Word Chan" and sweeping away Linji’s "Four Kinds of Selection. Departing from the precious seat in the morning, he reached Mount Zhong by evening;
like a ball rolling on a platter and a platter rolling a ball, with a single blow of his fist, he broke through Yuanwu’s barrier.

The ancient worthies’ proclamations were intended directly to stir up and elevate the ultimate point of the predecessors, thereby inspiring students.

From the outset, they had no intention of engaging in deliberate fabrication or arranging words and phrases. Yet, within their speech, there are moments of profound depth, extraordinary brilliance, and spontaneous perfection—truly formed as if by nature itself. This is because...
These arise from one's own authentic realization and are manifested as sounds; those who are ignorant do not understand this, and often act in the opposite manner.

Lake (Qingmao) Inscription:
The Patriarch’s method of direct pointing and singular upholding is the Dharma of the supreme vehicle of the one mind—a thunderclap in the blue sky, a tempest on dry land.
From the tip of the whisk, ten billion golden lions suddenly emerge; with a single snap of the fingers, ten billion Mount Sumerus are toppled in alarm.

Master Yuejiang appears and disappears in seven ways and eight manners, manifesting a thousand transformations and ten thousand shifts, following in the footsteps of the Linji school’s ancestral style.
Revealing the Eye of Yangqi, possessing great knowledge and vision, with the true medicine appearing before one: salt is salty and ginger is pungent;
one certainly knows that the opening of the mouth does not reside on the tongue. At the beginning of summer in the Renxu year of the Zhi-zhi era, Jinghai of Jingci respectfully inscribed this.

In the first month of summer in the year of Yihai of the Zhiyuan era, while residing at Shuanggui in the south, I was able to behold the records of his six assemblies of discourse. Thereupon, I joined my palms and said:
